{"reasoning_steps": ["The parabola opens upward in the figure so a>0.", "The parabola crosses the y-axis at the visible point (0,c).", "The drawn line passes through that same y-axis point so the line has y-intercept c and can be written y=mx+c for some slope m.", "The line also meets the parabola at a second point on the x-axis left of the origin so that second intersection has y=0.", "Equating parabola and line gives a x^2+(b-m)x=0 so the intersections occur at x=0 and x=(m-b)/a.", "The second intersection being on the x-axis gives (m-b)/a = -c/m.", "Thus the slope m must satisfy m^2 - b m + a c = 0.", "Testing m equal to a, b, or c yields conditions a(a-b+c)=0, a c=0, or c(c-b+a)=0 respectively.", "Those algebraic conditions require relations among a, b, and c that are not visible or determinable from the figure.", "The visible information is insufficient to determine which provided linear equation is the line."], "answer": "insufficient information"}

{"reasoning_steps":["The diagram shows seven small triangles with the perimeters labeled 10, 9, 15, 13, 12, 11, and 20.","The sum of those seven labeled perimeters is 10+9+15+13+12+11+20 = 90.","For any triangulation of a triangle the sum of the perimeters of the small triangles equals the perimeter of the large triangle plus twice the total length of all internal segments.","The internal segments visible in the partition together form lengths that, taken collectively, equal the perimeter of the large triangle.","Substituting those relations gives 90 = P + 2P = 3P where P is the large triangle's perimeter.","Solving 3P = 90 gives P = 30."],"answer":"30"}

{"reasoning_steps": ["Top row second cell reads '16'.", "Top row fourth cell reads '22'.", "Second row first cell reads '20'.", "Second row third cell reads '21'.", "Second row fifth cell reads '2'.", "Third row second cell reads '25'.", "Third row fourth cell reads '1'.", "Fourth row first cell reads '24'.", "Fourth row third cell reads '5'.", "Fourth row fifth cell reads '6'.", "Fifth row second cell reads '4'.", "Let S denote the common sum of each row and each column.", "Column two sum equals S.", "Column two sum equals 16 + d + 25 + i + 4.", "Therefore d + i equals S - 45.", "Row two sum equals S.", "Row two sum equals 20 + d + 21 + e + 2.", "Therefore d + e equals S - 43.", "Subtracting the relation d + i = S - 45 from d + e = S - 43 yields e - i = 2.", "Therefore e equals i + 2.", "Row four sum equals S.", "Row four sum equals 24 + i + 5 + j + 6.", "Therefore i + j equals S - 35.", "Column four sum equals S.", "Column four sum equals 22 + e + 1 + j + ?.", "Therefore e + j + ? equals S - 23.", "Replacing e by i + 2 and using i + j = S - 35 in e + j + ? = S - 23 yields ? = 10.", "Therefore the number in the cell marked with a question mark is 10."], "answer": "10"}

{"reasoning_steps":["The figure shows one continuous string with three crossing points each covered by a coin arranged roughly triangularly.","Under each coin the crossing can be one of two over/under choices as illustrated in image1 and image2.","The three choices are independent so there are 2^3 = 8 equally likely crossing configurations.","Any nontrivial knot formed by a diagram with three crossings must be a trefoil or its mirror because the trefoil is the only knot with crossing number three.","When all three crossings have the same over/under orientation the projection is an alternating three-crossing diagram which corresponds to a trefoil knot.","There are exactly two configurations with all three crossings the same (all three one way or all three the other way).","The remaining six mixed-sign configurations deform to the unknot by Reidemeister moves or by visual simplification.","Therefore the probability the string is knotted after pulling the ends is 2/8 = 1/4."], "answer":"B"}

{"reasoning_steps":["The pup walking away at constant speed indicates x increases uniformly.","The diagram labels y as the roll thickness corresponding to the roll radius.","The remaining wrapped paper area is proportional to the remaining paper length.","Annular area is proportional to the square of the roll radius.","Therefore the roll radius is proportional to the square root of the remaining paper length.","Remaining paper length equals an initial constant minus x.","The square-root relation causes y to decrease slowly for small x and more steeply as x approaches the maximum unrolled length.","Option E visually matches a slow initial decrease followed by a steeper drop while A, B, C, and D do not match that shape."], "answer":"E"}

{"reasoning_steps":["The area of square PQRS is 36, so its side length is 6.","The area of square TUVR is 16, so its side length is 4.","Place PQRS with S=(0,0), R=(6,0), Q=(6,6), and P=(0,6) to match the diagramal adjacency.","Square TUVR has R as its bottom-left, so R=(6,0), V=(10,0), U=(10,4), and T=(6,4).","Square UWXY has U as its top-left and side length s, so X has coordinates (10+s,4-s).","P, T and X are collinear, so P=(0,6), T=(6,4), and X=(10+s,4-s) lie on one line.","The line through P and T has equation y=6-x/3, so substituting X gives 4-s = 6-(10+s)/3.","Solving 4-s = 6-(10+s)/3 yields s=2, so UWXY has side length 2.","Thus P=(0,6), V=(10,0) and X=(12,2) are the triangle vertices.","The area of triangle PXV is 1/2|0*(2-0)+12*(0-6)+10*(6-2)| = 16."],"answer":"16"}

{"reasoning_steps": ["The plot shows the graph of f on the square grid with x and y ticks at integers from -5 to 5.", "The curve crosses the x-axis three times at about x ≈ -1.5, x ≈ 2.2, and x ≈ 4.3 so f has three distinct zeros r1, r2, r3 at those x-values.", "f(f(x)) = 0 means f(x) must equal one of the zeros r1, r2, r3.", "I count intersections of the graph with the horizontal line y = r1 and find two intersection points on the left branch.", "I count intersections of the graph with the horizontal line y = r2 and find three intersection points (left ascent, central descent, right rising branch).", "I count intersections of the graph with the horizontal line y = r3 and find one intersection point on the far right branch.", "Summing the intersection counts gives 2 + 3 + 1 = 6 distinct solutions."], "answer": "6"}

{"reasoning_steps":["Top photo shows pairings A-d, B-a, C-b, D-c, E-e.","Bottom photo shows pairings A-b, B-e, C-d, D-a, E-c.","Let p denote the true mother-child mapping as a permutation of {a,b,c,d,e}.","p matches exactly two top-photo pairings.","p matches exactly three bottom-photo pairings.","If p matches the bottom-photo pairing for B then p(B)=e.","If p matches the bottom-photo pairing for D then p(D)=a.","If p matches the bottom-photo pairing for E then p(E)=c.","Taking p(B)=e, p(D)=a, and p(E)=c leaves children b and d unassigned for A and C.","Assigning the remaining children to match the top-photo pairings gives p(A)=d and p(C)=b.","The resulting p has two matches with the top photo (A and C).","The resulting p has three matches with the bottom photo (B, D, and E).","Therefore child a belongs to mother D."], "answer": "D"}

{"reasoning_steps": ["The problem statement and image show a solid with 12 regular pentagonal faces and the other faces being equilateral triangles or squares.", "The statement also specifies each pentagonal face is surrounded by 5 square faces and each triangular face is surrounded by 3 square faces.", "The pictured solid and adjacency information match the rhombicosidodecahedron.", "The rhombicosidodecahedron has 12 pentagonal faces, 20 triangular faces, and 30 square faces.", "Thus the solid has 12 pentagons, 20 triangles, and 30 squares.", "John writes 5 on each pentagon, giving a total from pentagons of 5*12 = 60.", "John writes 1 on each triangle, giving a total from triangles of 1*20 = 20.", "John writes -1 on each square, giving a total from squares of -1*30 = -30.", "The overall total is 60 + 20 + (-30) = 50."], "answer": "50"}

{"reasoning_steps": ["The circle has 15 equally spaced points on its circumference.", "The number of 3-point selections without symmetry is C(15,3) = 455.", "The problem identifies triangles under rotations and reflections so the symmetry group is the dihedral group of order 30.", "By Burnside's lemma the number of distinct triangles equals the average number of 3-point sets fixed by group elements.", "The identity rotation fixes all 455 triples.", "A nontrivial rotation can fix a 3-point set only if every rotation cycle has length dividing 3.", "That divisibility occurs only when gcd(15,k)=5, i.e., for rotations by 5 and 10 positions.", "Each of those two rotations partitions the points into 5 cycles of length 3 and thus fixes 5 triples each.", "All other nonidentity rotations fix no 3-point sets.", "Each reflection for odd n=15 fixes one vertex and swaps the other 14 points into 7 pairs.", "Each reflection therefore fixes triangles made of the fixed vertex together with one symmetric pair, giving 7 fixed triples per reflection.", "Summing fixed counts gives 455 + 2*5 + 15*7 = 570 and dividing by 30 yields 570/30 = 19."], "answer": "19"}

{"reasoning_steps": ["The diagram shows triangle ABC with two straight lines from vertices A and B intersecting inside the triangle.", "The intersection of the two cevians divides the big triangle into four smaller triangles with areas labelled 1, 3, 3 and an unknown x.", "The cevian from A to BC splits ABC into two subtriangles ABD and ADC, and the picture shows ABD contains the small triangles of areas 1 and 3.", "Therefore the area of ABD is 1 + 3 = 4.", "The other subtriangle ADC contains the small triangle of area 3 and the unknown area x, so ADC has area 3 + x.", "The cevian from B to AC splits ABC into ABE and BEC, and ABE contains the two small triangles of area 3 and 3 so ABE has area 6 while BEC has area 1 + x.", "The two small triangles at vertex A (one in ABD and one in ADC) are both labelled 3 so they have equal area, which implies BD = DC and hence ABD = ADC, so 4 = 3 + x.", "Solving 4 = 3 + x gives x = 1, and the total area is 1 + 3 + 3 + 1 = 8."], "answer": "8"}

{"reasoning_steps": ["The diagram shows mirrors OP and OQ meeting at O with OQ drawn horizontal and the point R marked on OQ with OR = 5 cm.", "The incident ray XY is drawn parallel to OQ at a perpendicular distance d from OQ.", "Let the acute angle between OQ and OP be α and use the reflection rule for direction angles φ' = 2θ - φ.", "Following the three reflections in order yields the final ray direction φ3 = 4α - 180°.", "The final ray meets OQ at right angles so φ3 = 90°, which gives 4α - 180° = 90° and hence α = 67.5°.", "Reflecting the point R(a,0) across OP, then OQ, then OP gives the image R''' = (a cos 4α, a sin 4α).", "The incoming ray is horizontal at y = d so d equals the y-coordinate of R''' and therefore d = a sin 4α.", "Substituting a = 5 cm and α = 67.5° gives sin 4α = sin 270° = -1.", "Therefore the magnitude of d is 5 cm."], "answer": "C"}

{"reasoning_steps": ["The original diagram (image1) shows four horizontal bars decreasing top-to-bottom with the top bar longest and the bottom bar shortest.", "The dotted vertical grid in the images provides discrete alignment positions for bar ends.", "The problem statement says two apps this week have exactly half their previous time and two apps have the same time as last week.", "Halving an original bar would place its end on a grid position that is exactly halfway along its original length on the same dotted grid.", "In option D the second bar from the top is visibly shorter than the bottom bar.", "In the original the second bar from the top is visibly longer than the bottom bar.", "If the second original bar were halved it would align with the same grid tick as the original bottom bar in the original diagram and thus could not be strictly shorter on the same grid.", "Because option D shows the second bar strictly shorter than the bottom bar it cannot be produced by halving two of the original bars and leaving two unchanged under the given grid alignment."], "answer": "D"}

{"reasoning_steps": ["The diagram shows A, B, C, D placed left-to-right on a straight line in that order.", "AC is given as 12 cm, so the distance from A to C is 12 cm.", "BD is given as 18 cm, so the distance from B to D is 18 cm.", "Place A at coordinate 0 and C at coordinate 12 on the line to reflect AC = 12.", "Let B be at coordinate b.", "Let D be at coordinate d.", "From BD = 18 we have d - b = 18.", "The left-to-right order implies 0 < b < 12 < d.", "The midpoint of AB is at b/2 and the midpoint of CD is at (12 + d)/2.", "The distance between the midpoints is |(12 + d)/2 - b/2| which equals (12 + d - b)/2.", "Substituting d - b = 18 gives the distance = (12 + 18)/2 = 30/2 = 15 cm."], "answer": "E"}

{"reasoning_steps":["The diagram shows four straight lines intersecting at one point.","The lines form eight equal angles, each measuring 45°.","The small grey circle at the center has a radius that spans about one grid square as seen against the background grid.","The outer black arc labeled B clearly subtends a quarter of its circle, corresponding to 90°.","The center of arc B lies on a circle whose radius spans about four grid squares from the center as seen on the grid.","The length of arc B equals (90°/360°)·2π·(4·r_small) which simplifies to 2π·r_small.","The circumference of the little grey circle equals 2π·r_small.","Therefore arc B has the same length as the circumference of the little grey circle."], "answer":"B"}

{"reasoning_steps": ["Read text: \"91.876 m^3\".", "The five displayed digits are 9, 1, 8, 7, 6.", "These five digits are currently all different.", "The meter advances by 0.001 m^3 per increment.", "To reach 92.000 requires adding 0.124 m^3.", "Any reading with integer part 91 would have fixed digits 9 and 1 so no decimal digit may equal 9 or 1.", "All decimal triples from 877 through 999 either include 9 or 1 or have repeated digits, so no valid reading occurs before 92.000.", "The reading 92.000 has digits 9, 2, 0, 0, 0 with repeated zeros and is invalid.", "We then check readings after 92.000 for the first reading with five distinct digits.", "The reading 92.013 has digits 9, 2, 0, 1, 3 which are all different.", "No earlier reading between 92.000 and 92.012 has all five digits different because of repeated zeros or a repeated 2.", "The difference from 91.876 to 92.013 is 0.137 m^3."], "answer": "D"}

{"reasoning_steps":["The big square is partitioned by one vertical and one horizontal line that are equidistant from the top and left edges, producing two squares (top-left and bottom-right) and two rectangles.","Let the big square side length be L and let the interior lines be a units from the top and left edges.","Then the top-left square has side a and the bottom-right square has side L - a.","The shaded quadrilateral has vertices at the midpoints of the inner sides: the right and bottom sides of the top-left square and the left and top sides of the bottom-right square.","Those midpoint coordinates relative to the top-left corner are (a/2,a), (a,a/2), ((a+L)/2,a), and (a,(a+L)/2).","Computing its area by the shoelace formula gives area = L^2/8.","The shaded area is given as 3, so L^2/8 = 3.","Hence L^2 = 24 and the big square area is 24.","The non-shaded area equals total minus shaded, 24 - 3 = 21."], "answer":"21"}

{"reasoning_steps": ["The diagram shows 16 towns arranged in a 4×4 square lattice with roads connecting horizontally and vertically adjacent towns.", "Each power plant supplies the town it occupies and all towns connected to it by a single road as stated.", "An interior town in this lattice has 4 neighbours and a plant there can cover up to 5 towns, an edge non-corner town has 3 neighbours and a plant there can cover up to 4 towns, and a corner town has 2 neighbours and a plant there can cover up to 3 towns.", "Three plants can therefore cover at most 3×5=15 towns without accounting for overlaps, which is less than 16 so at least 4 plants are required.", "Placing plants at the top-row second-from-left town, the second-row rightmost town, the third-row leftmost town, and the bottom-row second-from-right town covers every town because each town is either a plant or adjacent to one."], "answer": "4"}

{"reasoning_steps":["The image shows a rectangular cuboid subdivided into a 3x3x3 grid of smaller cuboids.","That subdivision implies two planes parallel to each pair of faces resulting in three slices along each of the three dimensions.","Let the original cuboid dimensions be a, b, c as suggested by visible orthogonal edges.","The original surface area is X = 2(ab + bc + ac).","Each small cuboid has dimensions ai, bj, ck with sums a = sum_i ai, b = sum_j bj, c = sum_k ck.","The total surface area equals 2 times the sum over all small cuboids of (ai*bj + bj*ck + ck*ai).","The sum over all i,j,k of ai*bj equals 3ab because summing over the third index gives a factor of 3.","Similarly the other two double-products sum to 3bc and 3ca respectively.","Therefore the total surface area is 2*3*(ab + bc + ca) = 3*2(ab + bc + ca) = 3X.","Thus the correct choice is \"C\"."], "answer": "C"}

{"reasoning_steps": ["The diagram shows a circle centered at (0,0) with axis ticks marked to 5.", "The circle's radius is 5 so integer-coordinate points on the circumference satisfy x^2 + y^2 = 25.", "The equation 5^2 + 0^2 = 25 yields the integer-coordinate points (5,0) and (-5,0).", "The equation 0^2 + 5^2 = 25 yields the integer-coordinate points (0,5) and (0,-5).", "The Pythagorean identity 3^2 + 4^2 = 25 yields integer-coordinate points (3,4), (3,-4), (-3,4), (-3,-4).", "The identity 4^2 + 3^2 = 25 yields integer-coordinate points (4,3), (4,-3), (-4,3), (-4,-3).", "Counting distinct points 2 + 2 + 4 + 4 gives 12 integer-coordinate points on the circumference."], "answer": "12"}

{"reasoning_steps": ["The diagram shows one central vertical column of 9 equal small rectangles stacked and one larger rectangle on each side, giving 11 rectangles in total.", "The bottom side of a smallest rectangle is labeled \"1\" in the figure, so each smallest rectangle has width 1.", "All small rectangles are similar to the original rectangle as stated in the problem.", "Let r denote the height-to-width ratio of the original rectangle, so each smallest rectangle has height r and width 1.", "The 9 stacked smallest rectangles fill the full height of the big rectangle, so the big rectangle height H equals 9r.", "Each side rectangle extends from the top to the bottom of the big rectangle, so each side rectangle has height H.", "A rectangle similar to the original that has height H must be a rotated copy with scale factor a satisfying a*W = H where W is the big rectangle width, so a = H/W = r.", "For such a rotated side rectangle its width equals a*H, so each side rectangle width equals r*H.", "The total width W of the big rectangle equals the central column width 1 plus the two side widths 2*(r*H), so W = 1 + 2rH.", "Substituting H = 9r into W = 1 + 2rH gives W = 1 + 18 r^2.", "The aspect ratio r satisfies H/W = r, so (9r)/(1+18 r^2) = r.", "Dividing by r gives 9 = 1 + 18 r^2.", "Solving 18 r^2 = 8 yields r^2 = 4/9 and r = 2/3.", "Then H = 9r = 6 and W = 1 + 18 r^2 = 9.", "The perimeter of the big rectangle is 2*(W+H) = 2*(9+6) = 30."], "answer": "30"}

{"reasoning_steps":["The diagram shows a bottom rectangle labeled \"5\" for its horizontal length and the right slanted side has a segment labeled \"1\" adjacent to it.","The diagram shows an upper rectangle labeled \"3\" for its horizontal length and the right slanted side has a segment labeled \"2\" above the \"1\" segment.","The labels on the slanted side indicate the bottom rectangle has height 1 and the upper rectangle has height 2 so the upper rectangle top is at height 3 above the base.","Let W be the horizontal distance from the common left vertical edge of the rectangles to the right slanted side at the base and let H be the triangle height from the base to A.","By similarity the horizontal width at height y equals W*(1 - y/H).","The width at height y=1 equals 5 so W*(1 - 1/H) = 5.","The width at height y=3 equals 3 so W*(1 - 3/H) = 3.","Subtracting the two equations gives W*(2/H) = 2, which implies W/H = 1.","Substituting W = H into W*(1 - 1/H) = 5 gives H - 1 = 5, hence H = 6.","The computed triangle height H = 6 is not among options A–D."],"answer":"E"}

{"reasoning_steps": ["The diagram shows ten circles filled with the numbers 1 through 10 and labels the left column sum 24, the right column sum 24, and the bottom row sum 25.", "Label the top-center questioned circle T and the bottom-center circle B.", "The sum of the numbers 1 through 10 equals 55.", "The eight column circles sum to 24 + 24 = 48, so T + B = 55 - 48 = 7.", "Therefore B must be an integer from 1 to 6 and T = 7 - B.", "From the bottom-row equation L4 + B + R4 = 25 we get L4 + R4 = 25 - B.", "If B = 1,2,3,4,5 then L4 + R4 would be 24,23,22,21,20 respectively.", "No two distinct numbers from 1 to 10 can sum to any of 20 through 24 because the maximum possible sum of two distinct numbers is 10 + 9 = 19.", "If B = 6 then T = 1.", "If B = 6 then L4 + R4 = 19 and that can be achieved by the pair 10 and 9 from the remaining numbers.", "Therefore the only feasible value for the question-mark circle T is 1."], "answer": "E"}

{"reasoning_steps": ["Read the expression as 2^{0^{2^3}} + 0^{2^{3^2}} + 2^{3^{2^0}} + 3^{2^{0^2}} from the visible text.", "Interpret 0^{2^3} as 0^{8}.", "Compute 0^{8} = 0.", "Compute 2^{0} = 1 for the first term.", "Compute 3^{2} = 9 from the visible 3^2 in the second term's exponent.", "Compute 2^{9} = 512 for the second term's exponent.", "Compute 0^{512} = 0 for the second term.", "Compute 2^{0} = 1 for the inner exponent of the third term.", "Compute 3^{1} = 3 for the third term's exponent.", "Compute 2^{3} = 8 for the third term.", "Compute 0^{2} = 0 for the inner exponent of the fourth term.", "Compute 2^{0} = 1 for the fourth term's exponent.", "Compute 3^{1} = 3 for the fourth term.", "Sum the terms 1 + 0 + 8 + 3 = 12."], "answer": "12"}

{"reasoning_steps":["The diagram shows nine contiguous squares in a single row.","The second square from the left contains the digit 7.","The fourth square from the left contains the digit 9.","The rule that the sum of three adjacent numbers is always a multiple of 3 implies the residues r_i modulo 3 satisfy r_i+r_{i+1}+r_{i+2}≡0 (mod 3).","From that congruence we get the recurrence r_{i+2}≡-(r_i+r_{i+1}) (mod 3).","The numbers 1 through 9 provide exactly three residues of each class 0,1,2 modulo 3.","The recurrence determines the whole residue sequence from the initial pair (r1,r2).","If r1=r2 the recurrence gives a constant sequence of one residue and therefore fails the requirement of three of each residue.","If r1≠r2 the recurrence produces a repeating 0,1,2 3-cycle and thus yields three of each residue.","Because the second square contains 7, we must have r2=1.","Because the fourth square contains 9, we must have r4=0.","The only 3-cycle initial pair satisfying r2=1 and r4=0 is r1=0,r2=1, giving the residue pattern 0,1,2,0,1,2,0,1,2 for positions 1–9.","Residue-0 positions are 1,4,7 with 9 fixed at position 4 and {3,6} to place at positions 1 and 7 in 2! ways.","Residue-1 positions are 2,5,8 with 7 fixed at position 2 and {1,4} to place at positions 5 and 8 in 2! ways.","Residue-2 positions are 3,6,9 with {2,5,8} assignable to those three positions in 3! ways.","Therefore the total number of valid fillings is 2×2×6 = 24."], "answer":"24"}

{"reasoning_steps":["The figure is a triangular pyramid (tetrahedron) with six edges and four visible edge lengths labeled 2, 4, 3, and 7 around the outer cycle.","Label the cycle edges AB=2, BC=4, CD=3, DA=7 and denote the two unseen diagonals AC=x and BD=y.","Triangle ABC has side lengths 2, 4, and x, so by the triangle inequality |2-4|<x<2+4 giving x∈{3,4,5}.","Triangle CDA has side lengths 3, 7, and x, so by the triangle inequality |7-3|<x<7+3 giving x∈{5,6,7,8,9}.","Intersecting the two sets for x yields x=5.","Triangle BCD has side lengths 4, 3, and y, so by the triangle inequality |4-3|<y<4+3 giving y∈{2,3,4,5,6}.","Triangle DAB has side lengths 7, 2, and y, so by the triangle inequality |7-2|<y<7+2 giving y∈{6,7,8}.","Intersecting the two sets for y yields y=6.","The sum of the two missing side lengths x+y is 5+6=11."],"answer":"11"}

{"reasoning_steps":["The arrows on the outer ring show numbers increasing clockwise around the ring.","The top row of the outer ring shows 10→11→12→13 increasing to the right.","The right column of the outer ring shows 13↓14↓15↓16 increasing downward.","The bottom row of the outer ring shows 17←18←19←20←21 increasing to the left.","The left column of the outer ring shows 21↑22↑23↑24 increasing upward.","The diagram suggests 25 would lie at the top-left corner because arrows continue upward from 24.","The numbers after a top-left corner proceed to the right along the top row as shown by 10→11→12→13.","By analogy 625 = 25^2 would lie at the top-left corner of the 25×25 ring.","626 is immediately to the right of 625.","627 is immediately to the right of 626."],"answer":"C"}

{"reasoning_steps": ["Read visible text as the polynomial x^5 - 11x^4 + (illegible middle terms) - 7.", "The polynomial is monic of degree five with constant term -7.", "For a monic degree-5 polynomial the product of the five roots equals -constant term, which is 7.", "The problem states that all zeros are integers.", "Therefore each root must be an integer divisor of 7, so each root is in the set {±1, ±7}.", "Because the product of the five roots is 7, exactly one root must be ±7 and the other four roots must multiply to 1, so a+b = 1 where a and b count +7 and -7 respectively.", "The sum of the five roots equals 11 because the x^4 coefficient is -11.", "If the ±7 root is +7 then the remaining four roots must sum to 4 and multiply to 1, which forces them to be four 1's.", "If the ±7 root were -7 then the remaining four roots would have to sum to 18 which is impossible for four numbers each in {±1}.", "Hence the roots are 7,1,1,1,1.", "Therefore the root 1 has multiplicity 4 and (x-1)^4 divides the polynomial."], "answer": "D"}

{"reasoning_steps":["The big square is split into four equal small squares so each small square side equals S/2 if S is the big side length.","Place the origin at the midlines intersection so the vertical midline is x=0 and the right side is x=S/2.","The right side midpoint is at (S/2,0).","The circle touches the right side at that midpoint which implies the circle center lies on the horizontal midline and has x-coordinate S/2 - r.","The diagram labels 8 cm from the left border to the circle on the horizontal midline so the left intersection x-coordinate is -S/2 + 8.","The left horizontal intersection equals center_x minus r so S/2 - 2r = -S/2 + 8.","Solving S/2 - 2r = -S/2 + 8 gives r = (S - 8)/2 and hence the center_x equals 4 cm.","The diagram labels 6 cm from the top border to the circle on the vertical midline so that vertical intersection has y-coordinate S/2 - 6.","Points on the vertical midline satisfy center_x^2 + y^2 = r^2 so r^2 - 16 = (S/2 - 6)^2 because center_x = 4 cm.","Substituting r = S/2 - 4 into r^2 - 16 = (S/2 - 6)^2 and simplifying yields S = 18."],"answer":"A"}

{"reasoning_steps": ["The image shows four 3x3 corner blocks each with a central black square and white border squares.", "The board total count is 44 unit squares with 40 white squares and 4 black center squares as stated.", "The corner blocks contribute 8 white squares each giving 32 white squares in the four corners.", "The remaining 8 white squares appear as four 1x2 bridges connecting adjacent corner blocks.", "Each corner white region (a 3x3 without center) forms an 8-cycle of squares around the removed center.", "Each bridge has two covering options: a single domino covering the two bridge cells or two dominoes each pairing a bridge cell with its adjacent corner cell.", "If a bridge is covered internally then the two adjacent corner vertices remain available to tile inside their 8-cycle.", "If a bridge is covered externally then the two adjacent corner vertices are occupied and removed from the 8-cycle.", "A corner 8-cycle has 5 perfect matchings when both its adjacent bridge vertices are present.", "A corner 8-cycle has 3 perfect matchings when both its adjacent bridge vertices are removed.", "For each corner to be tileable the two incident bridges must be in the same state, which forces all four bridges to be in the same state.", "Summing the two global cases gives total tilings 5^4 + 3^4 = 625 + 81 = 706."], "answer": "706"}

{"reasoning_steps": ["The image shows four identical concentric-ring targets with three arrows on each target.", "On target 1 two arrowheads lie on the middle ring and one lies on the inner bullseye.", "On target 2 two arrowheads lie on the inner bullseye and one lies on the outer ring.", "On target 3 two arrowheads lie on the outer ring and one lies on the inner bullseye.", "Let the inner, middle and outer ring point values be C, B and A respectively.", "Target 1 yields the equation 2B + C = 29.", "Target 2 yields the equation A + 2C = 43.", "Target 3 yields the equation 2A + C = 47.", "Twice the second equation minus the third equation gives 3C = 39.", "From 3C = 39 we get C = 13.", "Substituting C into A + 2C = 43 gives A = 17.", "Substituting C into 2B + C = 29 gives B = 8.", "On target 4 the image shows one arrow on each ring.", "Target 4 score is A + B + C = 17 + 8 + 13 = 38."], "answer": "38"}

{"reasoning_steps": ["The figure shows a circle with a central white square and the surrounding area shaded inside the circle.", "The central white square appears inscribed in the circle because its four vertices touch the circle.", "The circle radius is given as 3 cm.", "The circle diameter is 6 cm and its area is 9π cm².", "The inscribed square diagonal equals the diameter 6 cm so the square side is 6/√2 = 3√2 cm.", "The square area is (3√2)² = 18 cm².", "The shaded area equals the circle area minus the square area = 9π - 18 cm².", "The expression 9π - 18 simplifies to 9(π - 2) which matches option D."], "answer": "D"}

{"reasoning_steps":["The diagram shows rectangle ABCD with A at bottom-left, B at bottom-right, C at top-right, and D at top-left.","Let the rectangle have width w and height h and place A=(0,0), B=(w,0), C=(w,h), D=(0,h).","Points P, Q, R, S are the midpoints of AB, BC, CD, and DA respectively as labeled.","Thus P=(w/2,0), Q=(w,h/2), R=(w/2,h), and S=(0,h/2).","T is the midpoint of segment RS as indicated by the figure, so T=((w/2+0)/2,(h+h/2)/2)=(w/4,3h/4).","The area of triangle PQT equals one half the absolute value of the determinant of vectors Q-P and T-P.","Q-P=(w/2,h/2) and T-P=(w/4-w/2,3h/4-0)=(-w/4,3h/4).","The determinant (w/2)*(3h/4)-(h/2)*(-w/4) equals wh/2.","Therefore the triangle area is 1/2*(wh/2)=wh/4 and the rectangle area is wh, so the fraction is (wh/4)/(wh)=1/4."],"answer":"B"}

{"reasoning_steps": ["The figure is a square divided into a 5 by 5 grid of equal small squares.", "Place M at coordinates (0,0).", "Each small square has side length 1.", "Then N is the point at (1,0).", "The top points A,B,C,D,E are at (1,5),(2,5),(3,5),(4,5),(5,5) respectively.", "For a top point P=(k,5) the slopes from P to M and N are 5/k and 5/(k-1) respectively.", "The angle M P N equals the difference arctan(5/k)-arctan(5/(k-1)).", "By the arctan subtraction formula this difference simplifies to arctan(5/(k(k-1)+25)).", "Evaluating for k=1..5 gives angles approximately 11.3099°, 10.4920°, 9.1677°, 7.6975°, and 6.3410°.", "The sum of these five angles is approximately 45.0081° which rounds to 45°."], "answer": "B"}

{"reasoning_steps":["Image shows isosceles triangles meeting at A with apex angle ∠BAC = 100°.","Each isosceles triangle has its two equal sides radiating from A and thus subtends a 100° angle at A.","Consecutive triangles share exactly one edge and therefore correspond to adjacent rays from A separated by 100°.","Label the rays from A by r0, r1, r2, ... so triangle k uses rays r_k and r_{k+1}.","After n steps the ray r_n is rotated by n·100° from r0.","Triangle n coincides with triangle 0 exactly when r_n = r0 and r_{n+1} = r1.","The condition r_n = r0 is equivalent to 100n ≡ 0 (mod 360).","Dividing by gcd(100,360)=20 gives 5n ≡ 0 (mod 18), whose smallest positive solution is n = 18.","Thus the first triangle that precisely covers triangle 0 is triangle number 18."], "answer":"18"}

{"reasoning_steps": ["O is the center of the circle at the intersection of the drawn perpendicular diameters.", "A rectangle sits with its left side on the vertical diameter and its right vertical side intersecting the circle at two points.", "The rectangle's horizontal side is labeled 4.", "The rectangle's diagonal from its lower-left corner to its upper-right corner is labeled 5.", "The diagonal has horizontal component 4 and length 5, so its vertical component is 3 by the Pythagorean relation.", "Let the lower right intersection have y-coordinate y and the upper right have y+3, and both satisfy x^2+y^2=r^2 with x=4, so (y+3)^2=y^2 which gives y=-3/2 and y+3=3/2.", "Substituting gives r^2 = 16+(3/2)^2 = 73/4 so the diameter is sqrt(73)."], "answer": "sqrt(73)"}

{"reasoning_steps":["The figure is a square ABCD with AB = 2 (given).","Place A at (0,2), B at (2,2), C at (2,0), and D at (0,0) to match the labeling and side length.","The semicircle with diameter AB has center at (1,2).","The semicircle with diameter AD has center at (0,1).","Each semicircle therefore has radius 1.","The two semicircles intersect at A and at O = (1,1), and O lies on diagonal AC.","The diagonal AC divides the square into two congruent right triangles of area 2 each.","The shaded area equals the square area 4 minus the sum of the two overlaps of the semicircles with the adjacent triangles.","The overlap of semicircle AB with triangle ABC equals ∫_0^1 x dx + ∫_1^2 sqrt(1-(x-1)^2) dx by vertical slicing between the line y=2-x and the semicircle y=2-√(1-(x-1)^2).","The integrals evaluate to 1/2 and π/4 respectively, so that overlap equals 1/2 + π/4.","By symmetry the two overlaps sum to 1 + π/2 and the shaded area equals 4 - (1 + π/2) = 3 - π/2."], "answer": "3 - π/2 (square units)"}

{"reasoning_steps":["The square has side length 6 and thus total area 36.","The dashed line through the figure is the line joining midpoints of opposite sides, so it is the horizontal line y=3.","Place coordinates with the bottom-left corner at (0,0) and the top-right corner at (6,6).","Let A=(a,3) and B=(b,3) with 0<=a<b<=6, consistent with A and B shown on the midline.","The figure shows lines from A and B to the opposite vertices (0,0) and (6,6).","The central polygon with vertices (0,0), A, (6,6), B has area given by the shoelace formula, which simplifies to 3(b-a).","The three parts are equal so each has area 36/3=12.","Setting 3(b-a)=12 gives b-a=4.","Thus the length AB equals 4."], "answer": "4"}

{"reasoning_steps": ["The provided image shows an 8x6 rectangular grid with two diagonals and 24 squares not cut by either diagonal.", "The total number of unit squares in an m by n grid is m*n.", "The number of unit squares a single corner-to-corner diagonal intersects is m + n - gcd(m,n).", "For an 8x6 grid gcd(8,6)=2 so each diagonal intersects 8+6-2=12 squares.", "The 8x6 total of 48 minus twice 12 equals 24 which matches the picture and shows the two diagonals share no common intersected square in that case.", "For a 10x6 grid m=10 and n=6 so gcd(10,6)=2 and each diagonal intersects 10+6-2=14 squares.", "The diagonals intersect at (m/2,n/2)=(5,3) which is a lattice vertex when m and n are even so they do not both pass through the interior of the same unit square.", "Therefore the number of squares cut by at least one diagonal is 2*14=28 and the number not cut equals total 60 minus 28 which is 32."], "answer": "32"}

{"reasoning_steps": ["Each small square has side length 2 cm.", "I take the lower-left visible grid intersection as the origin.", "Point D lies on the leftmost vertical gridline and five squares above the origin, so D=(0,5).", "Point A lies one square right and one square up from the origin, so A=(1,1).", "Point B lies five squares right on the bottom row, so B=(5,0).", "Point C lies eight squares right and three squares up from the origin, so C=(8,3).", "Compute sum1 = x1*y2 + x2*y3 + x3*y4 + x4*y1 = 1*0 + 5*3 + 8*5 + 0*1 = 55.", "Compute sum2 = y1*x2 + y2*x3 + y3*x4 + y4*x1 = 1*5 + 0*8 + 3*0 + 5*1 = 10.", "The area in grid-square units is 0.5*(sum1 - sum2) = 0.5*(55 - 10) = 22.", "Each grid square has area 4 cm^2, so the quadrilateral area is 22*4 = 88 cm^2."], "answer": "D"}

{"reasoning_steps":["The diagram shows a tetrahedron with vertices labeled A, B, C, D.","The edge AB is labeled 9 in the diagram.","The problem states that the ten labels used are the numbers 1 through 9 and 11 with 10 omitted.","Let the vertex labels be x, y, z, w for A, B, C, D respectively.","Each edge label equals the sum of the two vertex labels it connects.","Each vertex is incident to three edges so the sum of all six edge labels equals three times the sum of the four vertex labels.","Let Vsum denote the sum of the four vertex labels.","The sum of all six edge labels equals 3*Vsum.","The total of all ten labels equals Vsum + 3*Vsum = 4*Vsum.","The total of the numbers 1 through 9 and 11 equals 56.","Therefore Vsum = 56/4 = 14.","Given AB is labeled 9 we have x + y = 9.","Therefore z + w = 14 - 9 = 5.","Hence the edge CD equals z + w and is labeled 5."], "answer":"5"}

{"reasoning_steps":["The diagram labels rectangle ABCD with area 10.","I set coordinates A=(0,0), B=(w,0), C=(w,h), D=(0,h) so w*h=10.","M is the midpoint of AD as labeled.","N is the midpoint of BC as labeled.","M has coordinates (0,h/2).","N has coordinates (w,h/2).","Vertices of quadrilateral M B N D in order are (0,h/2), (w,0), (w,h/2), (0,h).","Shoelace sum1 = 0*0 + w*(h/2) + w*h + 0*(h/2) = 3wh/2.","Shoelace sum2 = (h/2)*w + 0*w + (h/2)*0 + h*0 = wh/2.","Area = 1/2*(sum1 - sum2) = 1/2*(wh) = wh/2.","Since wh = 10 the quadrilateral area equals 5."], "answer":"5"}

{"reasoning_steps": ["The diagram marks AD as the angle bisector at A with two equal angles labeled α beside AB and AC.", "The diagram marks BH as a height from B to AC with a right-angle marker at H indicating BH ⟂ AC.", "The diagram labels the obtuse angle between BH and AD as 4α.", "The angle from AD to AC equals α because AD bisects ∠CAB.", "The angle from AC to BH equals 90° because BH is perpendicular to AC.", "The obtuse angle from AD to BH equals α + 90° as it passes through AC.", "Setting α + 90° = 4α gives 90° = 3α and hence α = 30°.", "Therefore ∠CAB = 2α = 60°."], "answer": "C"}

{"reasoning_steps": ["The 3x3 grid shows 1 at top-left, 3 at top-right, 2 at bottom-left, and 4 at bottom-right.", "The remaining digits to place are 5, 6, 7, 8, and 9.", "If 9 were center then its four neighbours would be 5, 6, 7, 8 whose sum is 26 and not 15.", "If 9 were at the top-middle then its neighbours would be 1, 3, and the center and 1+3+center=15 would force the center to be 11 which is impossible.", "If 9 were at the middle-left then its neighbours would be 1, 2, and the center and 1+2+center=15 would force the center to be 12 which is impossible.", "If 9 were at the bottom-middle then its neighbours would be 2, 4, and the center and 2+4+center=15 would force the center to be 9 which violates uniqueness.", "Therefore 9 must be at middle-right and the center must be 8.", "The remaining three blanks are then 5, 6, and 7 which are the other neighbours of 8.", "The sum of the numbers neighbouring 8 is 9+5+6+7=27."], "answer": "27"}

{"reasoning_steps":["The provided tile image shows a square divided by its two diagonals into four congruent triangular regions with three dark triangles and one light triangle.","There are 5×5 tiles so there are 25 tiles and therefore 25 light triangles in the whole arrangement.","A border triangle is any small triangle that touches the exterior of the large 5×5 square, and counting such triangles gives 36 border triangles.","The 3×3 interior block of 9 tiles cannot contribute any light triangles to the exterior border because their triangles do not touch the exterior.","Thus a crude upper bound without adjacency constraints is that at most 25−9 = 16 border triangles could be light.","The edge-matching condition forces adjacency constraints on the quadrant in which a tile's single light triangle may lie, and these constraints form a 4-cycle relation among the four quadrant choices.","As a result the tiles fall into two parity classes on the checkerboard of the 5×5 grid where one class may choose only two opposite quadrant positions and the other class may choose the other two quadrant positions.","A border tile can put its light on the exterior only if its parity-allowed quadrant choices include a quadrant that touches that particular exterior side.","Checking the 16 border tiles under these parity restrictions shows exactly 13 border tiles have a non-empty intersection of parity-allowed choices with exterior-touching quadrants.","Therefore at most 13 border triangles can be light under the adjacency constraints.","Hence at least 36−13 = 23 of the border triangles must be dark.","The parity-based choices on individual tiles are independent across edges and hence the bound 23 is achievable by choosing each eligible border tile to place its light on an exterior quadrant.","Therefore the smallest possible number of dark triangles on the border is 23."], "answer":"23"}

{"reasoning_steps":["The picture shows two twig types with one twig having exactly five leaves and the other twig having exactly two leaves plus a flower.","The problem text states the bush has 10 twigs.","Let x be the number of twigs with five leaves and y be the number of twigs with two leaves and a flower.","The twig counts satisfy x + y = 10.","The total number of leaves equals 5x + 2y.","Substituting y = 10 - x gives total leaves = 5x + 2(10 - x).","Simplifying yields total leaves = 3x + 20.","For integer x from 0 to 10 the possible totals are 20, 23, 26, 29, 32, 35, 38, 41, 44, 47, and 50.","None of the options 45, 39, 37, or 31 appears in that list.","Therefore the correct choice is E."], "answer":"E"}

{"reasoning_steps":["The image shows a grid of dots and four labeled cars A (bottom-left), B (top-left), C (top-right), and D (middle-right).","Each car has an arrow showing its displacement in 5 seconds: A points up-right toward the center, B points down-right toward the center, C points straight down toward the center, and D points left toward the center.","The arrow paths of A and B visibly cross at the same left-of-center grid point.","The arrow paths of C and D visibly cross at the same right-of-center grid point.","The distance from A and B to their crossing point is visibly shorter than the distance from C and D to their crossing point.","Because the arrows show equal-time displacements, the pair with the shorter approach distance will meet first, so A and B collide before C and D."],"answer":"A"}

{"reasoning_steps": ["The diagram shows a rhombus with four corner points top, right, bottom, and left.", "The visible side labels are 8 on the top-left side, 9 on the top-right side, and 13 on the bottom-right side while the bottom-left side is labeled '?'.", "Let the corner numbers be A at top, B at right, C at bottom, and D at left.", "The problem states each side label equals the sum of its endpoint corner numbers.", "From the top-left side labeled 8 we have A + D = 8.", "From the top-right side labeled 9 we have A + B = 9.", "From the bottom-right side labeled 13 we have B + C = 13.", "From A + B = 9 we get A = 9 - B.", "Substituting gives D = B - 1 from A + D = 8, and C = 13 - B from B + C = 13.", "Therefore C + D = (13 - B) + (B - 1) = 12, so the '?' equals 12."], "answer": "12"}

{"reasoning_steps": ["The diagram shows a 2-row by 4-column grid with the dark field in the top-right cell.", "The visible numbers are 4 in the top second cell, 3 in the bottom first cell, and 8 in the bottom third cell.", "The numbers 1 through 8 sum to 36.", "Equal row sums imply each row must sum to 18.", "Equal column sums imply each column must sum to 9.", "Column 1 has 3 in the bottom cell so the top-left cell must be 6.", "Column 2 has 4 in the top cell so the bottom second cell must be 5.", "Column 3 has 8 in the bottom cell so the top third cell must be 1.", "The remaining unused numbers are 2 and 7.", "The top row sum 6+4+1+X must equal 18 so X must be 7.", "Therefore the dark top-right field must contain 7."], "answer": "7"}

{"reasoning_steps":["The image shows digits 0–9 constructed in a seven-segment style with one matchstick per segment.","In that depiction each visible segment corresponds to one matchstick so standard seven-segment counts apply.","The matchstick counts visible are 0=6, 1=2, 2=5, 3=5, 4=4, 5=5, 6=6, 7=3, 8=7, 9=6.","A positive whole number cannot have a leading zero so the first digit must be 1–9.","The total available matchsticks is 6 so the number of digits is at most three because 3×2=6 is the minimum cost.","Single-digit valid numbers use one digit with cost 6 and those digits are 6 and 9.","Two-digit numbers require two digits whose matchstick costs add to 6 with a nonzero first digit.","The only cost pairs summing to 6 are (2,4), (3,3), and (4,2).","Those pairs yield the two-digit numbers 14, 77, and 41 with first digits nonzero.","Three-digit numbers require three digits of cost 2 each and thus only 111 is possible.","Counting possibilities gives 2 single-digit + 3 two-digit + 1 three-digit = 6 valid positive numbers."],"answer":"6"}

{"reasoning_steps": ["Tom's diagram shows three hits in the inner circle, one hit in the middle ring, and two hits in the outer ring.", "John's diagram shows one hit in the inner circle, three hits in the middle ring, and two hits in the outer ring.", "Lily's diagram shows two hits in the inner circle, two hits in the middle ring, and two hits in the outer ring.", "Let the inner circle be A points, the middle ring be B points, and the outer ring be C points.", "Tom's hits give the equation 3A + B + 2C = 46.", "John's hits give the equation A + 3B + 2C = 34.", "Subtracting John's equation from Tom's gives 2A - 2B = 12.", "Therefore A - B = 6.", "Substituting A = B + 6 into John's equation yields 4B + 2C = 28.", "Therefore 2B + C = 14.", "From A = B + 6 and 2B + C = 14 we deduce A + B + C = 20.", "Lily's hits total 2A + 2B + 2C, which equals 2(A + B + C).", "Therefore Lily's score is 2 × 20 = 40."], "answer": "40"}

{"reasoning_steps": ["The picture shows two perpendicular rays with vertex S that form a 90° angle.", "The required angles 10°,20°,…,80° correspond to integer distances 1..8 on a 0..9 scale of tens of degrees.", "Model ray directions as integer marks in {0,1,…,9} with 0 and 9 already present for the given perpendicular rays.", "A required angle of k·10° is realized exactly when the mark set contains two numbers at distance k.", "To realize distances 8,7,6,5 one must include at least one element from each complementary pair {1,8},{2,7},{3,6},{4,5} among the interior marks.", "The interior marks correspond to the rays drawn inside the right angle.", "Choosing at least one element from each of those four disjoint pairs therefore requires at least four interior marks.", "The set of marks {0,1,2,4,6,9} (i.e. adding rays at 10°,20°,40°,60°) yields all distances 1..8 by pairwise differences, so four interior marks suffice."], "answer": "4"}

{"reasoning_steps": ["The diagram shows isosceles triangle ABC with vertex B and the labeled angle ABC = 40°.", "Therefore the base angles at A and C are equal to (180° - 40°)/2 = 70°.", "The two small marked angles are ∠EAB and ∠DCA and I denote their common measure by α as indicated in the figure.", "Ray AE from A is inside the triangle and makes angle ∠BAE = α so ∠EAC = 70° - α.", "Ray CD from C is inside the triangle and makes angle ∠DCA = α so ∠BCD = 70° - α.", "Place A = (0,0) and C = (1,0) and place B at (0.5, 0.5·tan70°) consistent with the visible base AC and base angles of 70°.", "For a representative choice α = 10° the direction of AE is at angle 70° - α = 60° from the x-axis and the direction of CD is at angle 180° - α = 170° from the x-axis, which matches the rays shown in the figure.", "Solving the two line equations for AE and CD gives their intersection F ≈ (0.0932, 0.1614), which lies inside the triangle as the figure shows.", "The vectors FC and FE computed from those coordinates have dot product and lengths that give ∠CFE ≈ arccos(0.3412) ≈ 70°.", "Therefore the requested angle ∠CFE equals 70° and the correct multiple-choice answer is D."], "answer": "D"}

{"reasoning_steps": ["Read text '5 cm/min' on the left side of the triangle.", "Read text '15 cm/min' on the right side of the triangle.", "Read text '20 cm/min' on the base of the triangle.", "The diagram and problem statement indicate the triangle is equilateral so all three sides have equal length.", "Let the common side length be s.", "The total distance walked around the triangle is 3s.", "Time to traverse the first side is s/5 minutes.", "Time to traverse the second side is s/15 minutes.", "Time to traverse the third side is s/20 minutes.", "Total time equals s*(1/5 + 1/15 + 1/20) minutes.", "The sum 1/5 + 1/15 + 1/20 equals 19/60.", "Average velocity equals total distance divided by total time, giving 3s/[s*(19/60)].", "Simplifying yields average velocity 180/19 cm/min.", "Therefore the correct multiple-choice letter is C."], "answer": "C"}

{"reasoning_steps":["I see a central hexagonal field in the middle of the diagram.","I see two pentagonal fields attached at the top that meet at a vertex.","I see two pentagonal fields attached at the bottom that meet at a vertex.","I see a rectangular (square-like) field attached on the left side of the central hexagon.","I see a rectangular (square-like) field attached on the right side of the central hexagon.","The distinct fields that are clearly visible in the image total seven.","The problem statement asks to place the numbers 1 to 9 which requires nine fields.","The image as provided does not clearly show two of the nine fields or their locations.","The adjacency relations between all nine fields cannot be determined from the provided image.","Because the complete field layout and adjacencies are ambiguous from the image, the number of valid labelings cannot be computed."], "answer":"insufficient information"}

{"reasoning_steps":["Read yesterday counts: top house 8, bottom-left house 7, bottom-right house 5.","Read today counts: top house 6, bottom-left house 10, bottom-right house 4.","The arrow indicates the path between the top house and the bottom-left house.","Let x_AB denote mice from top to bottom-left, x_AC denote top to bottom-right, x_BA denote bottom-left to top, x_BC denote bottom-left to bottom-right, x_CA denote bottom-right to top, and x_CB denote bottom-right to bottom-left.","Outgoing counts give x_AB + x_AC = 8, x_BA + x_BC = 7, and x_CA + x_CB = 5.","Incoming counts give x_BA + x_CA = 6, x_AB + x_CB = 10, and x_AC + x_BC = 4.","From x_AB + x_CB = 10 and x_AB + x_AC = 8 we get x_AB = 10 - x_CB and x_AC = x_CB - 2.","Substituting x_AC into x_AC + x_BC = 4 yields x_BC + x_CB = 6.","The total along the arrow is x_AB + x_BA = (10 - x_CB) + (7 - x_BC) = 17 - (x_CB + x_BC) = 11."],"answer":"11 mice"}

{"reasoning_steps":["The image shows a vertical addition of 777, 77, 77, 77, and 7 equaling 1015.","The image therefore uses ten digit 7s in total (3+2+2+2+1=10).","A number made of k sevens equals 7*(10^k-1)/9.","For 2023 let x,y,z be the counts of 7, 77, and 777 respectively.","The digit-count constraint is x+2y+3z=19.","The sum constraint is 7/9*(9x+99y+999z)=2023, which gives 9x+99y+999z=2601.","Dividing by 9 yields x+11y+111z=289.","Subtracting the digit-count equation from that gives 9y+108z=270, which simplifies to y+12z=30.","The only nonnegative integer solution is z=2, y=6, x=1.","Thus he must use the number 77 six times."], "answer": "6"}

{"reasoning_steps":["The figure shows a regular hexagon partitioned into a smaller central regular hexagon and four surrounding quadrilaterals.","Two outer quadrilaterals are shaded in the image.","By symmetry the four surrounding quadrilaterals are congruent and therefore have equal areas.","Let x denote the area of the small hexagon and let q denote the area of one quadrilateral.","The given ratio of shaded area to small hexagon area becomes (2q)/x = 4/3 because two quadrilaterals are shaded.","Solving (2q)/x = 4/3 gives q = (2/3)x.","The area of the big hexagon equals x + 4q = x + 4*(2/3)x = (11/3)x.","Therefore the ratio (Area of the small hexagon)/(Area of the big hexagon) equals x/((11/3)x) = 3/11."],"answer":"A"}

{"reasoning_steps": ["The top numbers shown after the first throw are 6, 7 and 8.", "Jakob coloured those three top pieces red as stated in the text.", "The six written numbers are six consecutive integers and must therefore form one of the sets {3,4,5,6,7,8}, {4,5,6,7,8,9}, {5,6,7,8,9,10}, or {6,7,8,9,10,11}.", "The sum of the first-throw top numbers 6+7+8 equals 21.", "The second- and third-throw top sums 23 and 17 differ from 21 by +2 and -4 respectively, so some subset of coins must change the top sum by +2 and some subset must change it by -4.", "A coin flip changes the top sum by (opposite-face number) minus (red number) on that coin, so +2 and -4 must occur as such differences from the three opposite-face numbers.", "In the candidate set {4,5,6,7,8,9} the three opposite-face numbers are 4,5 and 9, and pairing 9 with 7 gives a difference of +2 while pairing 4 with 8 gives a difference of -4, so the observed +2 and -4 are attainable.", "Therefore the three white (opposite) numbers are 4, 5 and 9 and their sum is 18."], "answer": "18"}

{"reasoning_steps":["I see two horizontal parallel lines that set a constant vertical separation (call it h).","Each marked strip 1, 2, 3 connects these two lines and has its top intersection points separated by the horizontal distance a as shown by the arrows.","Strip 1 is a vertical rectangle between the lines with horizontal width a and area a*h.","Strip 2 is a parallelogram between the lines with slanted sides that are parallel and with top and bottom separations equal to a.","A shear parallel to the lines maps the rectangle to the slanted parallelogram and shearing preserves area, so strip 2 also has area a*h.","Strip 3 is formed by piecewise horizontal displacements of parts of the rectangle (visible as slanted segments) which is a cutting-and-sliding operation that does not change area.","Therefore all three strips have the same area equal to a times the distance between the parallel lines."],"answer":"A"}

{"reasoning_steps":["The left circle and the square are bounded by the same dashed horizontal lines.","The dashed lines show the circle's diameter equals the square's side.","Let the circle radius be r so the square side equals 2r and a=(2r)^2=4r^2.","Each circle's area equals b so b=πr^2.","The three circles are tangent and have collinear centers as shown.","A taut thread around the fixed circles forms the convex hull of the three disks, which is a capsule shape.","That capsule equals a rectangle of length 4r and width 2r plus two semicircles, giving area 4r·2r+πr^2=8r^2+πr^2.","Substituting a=4r^2 and b=πr^2 yields the enclosed area 2a+b."],"answer":"B"}

{"reasoning_steps": ["Read text: 'XX'.", "Read text: '+ YY'.", "Read text: 'ZZ'.", "Read text: 'ZYX'.", "The problem statement says each of X, Y and Z represents a different non-zero digit.", "The two-digit number XX equals 11 times X.", "The two-digit number YY equals 11 times Y.", "The two-digit number ZZ equals 11 times Z.", "Therefore XX + YY + ZZ equals 11*(X + Y + Z).", "The three-digit result ZYX equals 100*Z + 10*Y + X.", "Equating gives 11*(X + Y + Z) = 100*Z + 10*Y + X.", "Rearranging gives 10*X + Y = 89*Z.", "For Z = 1 the right-hand side is 89 which gives 10*X + Y = 89.", "For Z >= 2 the right-hand side is at least 178 which exceeds two digits and so is impossible.", "Solving 10*X + Y = 89 yields X = 8 and Y = 9 when digits are distinct and non-zero."], "answer": "8"}

{"reasoning_steps": ["Image shows four overlapping squares labeled 11, 9, 7, and 5.", "The two grey squares are the ones labeled 11 and 7 based on shading.", "The two black squares are the ones labeled 9 and 5 based on shading.", "Area of the square with side 11 is 121 square units.", "Area of the square with side 7 is 49 square units.", "Sum of the grey areas is 121 + 49 = 170 square units.", "Area of the square with side 9 is 81 square units.", "Area of the square with side 5 is 25 square units.", "Sum of the black areas is 81 + 25 = 106 square units.", "The grey sum exceeds the black sum by 170 - 106 = 64 square units."], "answer": "64 square units"}

{"reasoning_steps": ["The image shows four semicircles of radius 1 with their centres at the mid-points of the sides of a square.", "That placement implies the side length of the square is 2 and each semicircle centre is at distance 1 from the square centre.", "The shaded circle is centred at the square centre and touches each semicircular arc.", "The line from the square centre to a corner has length sqrt(2).", "Along that line the distances from the square centre to the tangency point of the small circle and from that tangency point to the corner sum to sqrt(2), and those distances are (1 - r) and 1 respectively.", "Solving sqrt(2) = (1 - r) + 1 gives r = sqrt(2) - 1."], "answer": "A"}

{"reasoning_steps":["The dashed vertical and horizontal lines indicate the point (4,4).","The right branch is a straight line through the origin at 45 degrees.","A 45-degree line through the origin corresponds to f(x)=x for x≥0.","The graph shows the points (-4,0), (-2,2), (0,0), and (-8,-4).","From the left and middle linear pieces we read f(x)=x+4 for x≤-2.","From the middle and right pieces we read f(x)=-x for -2≤x≤0.","Solving f(t)=0 with the piecewise formula gives t=-4 or t=0.","Solving f(u)=-4 with the piecewise formula gives u=-8.","Solving f(x)=-8 with the piecewise formula gives x=-12.","Therefore the solutions of f(f(f(x)))=0 are x=-12,-8,-4,0."], "answer":"C"}

{"reasoning_steps": ["Label AB = W and AD = H so the rectangle area WH = 36.", "The circle is tangent to AB and AD so its center O is at distance r from both sides and thus O has coordinates (r,r).", "The diagonal BD passes through (0,H) and (W,0) so its equation is Hx + Wy - WH = 0.", "The distance from O to BD equals r so |Hr + Wr - WH|/sqrt(H^2 + W^2) = r.", "Rearranging the distance equation gives WH - r(H + W) = r sqrt(H^2 + W^2).", "Set S = W + H and Q = sqrt(W^2 + H^2) so the previous equation is WH - rS = rQ.", "Compute S^2 - Q^2 = (W+H)^2 - (W^2+H^2) = 2WH so (S+Q)(S-Q) = 2WH, and since r = WH/(S+Q) we get S - Q = 2r.", "From S - Q = 2r we have Q = S - 2r.", "The rectangle O P C R has corners O(r,r), P(W,r), C(W,H), R(r,H) by the visible horizontal and vertical through O, so its area is (W - r)(H - r).", "Expand the area to get (W - r)(H - r) = WH - rS + r^2.", "Use WH - rS = rQ and Q = S - 2r to get WH - rS = rS - 2r^2 and hence WH = 2(rS - r^2).", "Therefore the rectangle area rS - r^2 equals WH/2 and substituting WH = 36 gives the area 36/2 = 18."], "answer": "18"}

{"reasoning_steps":["Place the rectangle in a coordinate plane with A=(0,0), B=(12,0), C=(12,6), D=(0,6).","The fold is along diagonal AC which has equation y=0.5x.","Reflecting B=(12,0) across AC gives B'=(7.2,9.6), matching the folded corner position shown in the diagram.","The folded triangles overlap in triangle A-C-P where P is the intersection of line AB' with the top edge y=6, giving P=(4.5,6).","Reflecting P across AC gives Q=(7.5,0) on the bottom edge AB.","After cutting the parts outside the overlap and unfolding, the remaining region is the union of triangles A-C-P and A-C-Q, i.e., quadrilateral A-Q-C-P.","The side lengths AQ, QC, CP, and PA are all equal to 7.5 as computed from the coordinates.","Hence the side length of the resulting rhombus is 15/2."],"answer":"15/2"}

{"reasoning_steps": ["The left 2x3 board shows a chessboard pattern with the top-left square black and adjacent squares alternating colors.", "The right board is the color-inverse of the left board where every black must become white and every white must become black.", "Each allowed step repaints two edge-adjacent squares and applies the cycle black -> green -> white -> black to each repainted square.", "Model colors as states 0=black,1=green,2=white so one repaint increments a square's state by 1 modulo 3.", "An initial white square (state 2) therefore needs a net increment of +1 mod 3 to become black and an initial black square (state 0) needs +2 mod 3 to become white.", "Label the six squares and the seven edges between adjacent squares and let each edge variable count how many times that edge is used, with each use adding 1 to its two endpoint squares modulo 3.", "Writing one congruence per square gives a linear system mod 3 that reduces to two free variables a and b with the other edge variables determined as e=2-a, g=2-b, c=a+2, d=b+2, f=1-a-b (all mod 3).", "Each edge variable can be taken as 0,1,2 and the total number of steps equals the sum of the seven edge-variable values as ordinary integers.", "Checking all nine choices for a and b in {0,1,2} yields achievable totals and the minimal total sum is 6."], "answer": "6"}

{"reasoning_steps": ["The diagram shows quadrilateral ABCD with diagonal AC drawn.", "The angle at B is labeled 75°.", "The angle between AC and CB at C is labeled 30°.", "The angle between AC and AD at A is labeled 50°.", "The problem statement gives BC = AD.", "In triangle ABC the angles at B and C are 75° and 30° so angle BAC = 75°.", "The interior angle at A of the quadrilateral is angle DAB = 50° + 75° = 125°.", "Quadrilateral interior angles sum to 360°.", "The interior angle at C equals 30° + angle ACD.", "From the angle sum we get angle ACD + angle ADC = 130°, so angle ACD = 130° - angle ADC.", "By the Law of Sines BC = AC * sin(BAC)/sin(ABC) and AD = AC * sin(ACD)/sin(ADC).", "From BC = AD and AC ≠ 0 we get sin(BAC)/sin(ABC) = sin(ACD)/sin(ADC).", "Since BAC = ABC = 75° the left ratio is 1 so sin(ACD) = sin(ADC).", "The sine equality gives ACD = ADC or ACD = 180° - ADC.", "The supplementary case 130° - x = 180° - x is impossible so ACD = ADC.", "Solving 130° - x = x gives x = 65°."], "answer": "D"}

{"reasoning_steps": ["The provided picture shows a small square grid with 1x1 squares colored along both main diagonals.", "The problem describes a 2003x2003 grid of 1x1 squares.", "The colored squares lie exactly on the two diagonals of the grid.", "For an odd n the central unit square lies on both diagonals.", "The number of distinct colored squares equals 2*2003-1.", "2*2003-1 equals 4005.", "The total number of unit squares equals 2003^2.", "The number of white squares equals 2003^2-4005.", "2003^2-4005 simplifies to 2002^2.", "Therefore the correct multiple-choice letter is A."], "answer": "A"}

{"reasoning_steps": ["The image shows a central black circle surrounded by two concentric rings.", "The outer ring is grey and the middle ring is white.", "The problem states that each ring width equals the radius of the black circle.", "Let r be the radius of the black circle.", "The radius to the outer edge of the white ring is 2r.", "The radius to the outer edge of the grey ring is 3r.", "The grey ring area equals π(3r)^2 − π(2r)^2 = 5πr^2.", "The inner black circle area equals πr^2.", "The grey ring area is 5 times the black circle area."], "answer": "5"}

{"reasoning_steps":["Points A and B lie on both circles, so CA = CB and DA = DB.","Let R denote the larger circle's radius CA = CB and let r denote the smaller circle's radius DA = DB.","Triangle ACB is isosceles with sides R and vertex angle ACB = 60° at C.","By the Law of Cosines in triangle ACB, AB^2 = R^2 + R^2 - 2R^2 cos60°, which simplifies to AB^2 = R^2.","Thus AB = R since AB is a length and nonnegative.","Triangle ADB is isosceles with legs r and vertex angle ADB = 90° at D.","By the Pythagorean relation in triangle ADB, AB^2 = r^2 + r^2 = 2 r^2.","Thus AB = r√2.","Equating the two expressions for AB gives R = r√2.","Therefore the larger radius is √2 times the smaller radius and the correct choice is B."], "answer":"B"}

{"reasoning_steps": ["Read text: Tank I base area = 2 dm^2, height = 10 cm, water height = 5 cm.", "Read text: Tank II base area = 1 dm^2, height = 7 cm, and it is empty and placed inside tank I.", "Convert units: 1 dm^2 = 100 cm^2, so A1 = 2 dm^2 = 200 cm^2 and A2 = 1 dm^2 = 100 cm^2.", "Initial water volume = A1 * initial height = 200 cm^2 * 5 cm = 1000 cm^3.", "The diagram shows tank II is open and water spills into it, so the water level is the same inside tank II and in the remainder of tank I.", "Therefore the final water volume equals final height h times the full base area A1, i.e., volume = A1 * h.", "Solve for h: h = 1000 cm^3 / 200 cm^2 = 5 cm.", "The final height 5 cm is less than tank II height 7 cm so tank II does not overflow."], "answer": "E"}

{"reasoning_steps":["The diagram labels the rope as 8 m and the two adjacent house sides as 6 m (top) and 4 m (side).","The house blocks a 90° sector from the anchor, leaving a 270° unobstructed arc of radius 8 m around the anchor.","An unobstructed arc of 270° around radius 8 m has length (3/4)*2π*8 = 12π m.","If the rope wraps around the top-right corner after running 6 m along the top, the remaining radius is 8-6 = 2 m giving a quarter-circle arc of radius 2 m.","If the rope wraps around the bottom-left corner after running 4 m down the side, the remaining radius is 8-4 = 4 m giving a quarter-circle arc of radius 4 m.","The two quarter-circle arc lengths are (1/4)*2π*2 = π m and (1/4)*2π*4 = 2π m, so all arcs sum to 12π+π+2π = 15π m.","The boundary also includes straight house-edge segments visible in the figure of lengths 6 m (top), 4 m (left), 2 m (right small portion), and 4 m (bottom small portion).","The straight segments total 6+4+2+4 = 16 m.","Therefore the total perimeter is 15π + 16 m, matching option A."],"answer":"A"}

{"reasoning_steps":["The triangular figure shows 4 rows of small squares with row lengths 1, 2, 3, 4.","Therefore the total side-length in small-square units is 4 from A to the base and from the base to B.","Each small square is divided by a top-left to bottom-right diagonal creating allowed down-right edges.","The inset arrows indicate allowed moves are down, right, and down-right along those small-triangle sides.","Model positions by integer coordinates (i,j) with i counting down steps and j counting right steps starting at A=(0,0).","A diagonal step increases both i and j by 1 and leaves i-j unchanged.","To reach B one must have i=4 and j=4 so if k is the number of diagonal steps then s+k=4 and e+k=4 where s is the number of pure down steps and e is the number of pure right steps.","Hence s=e=4-k for k=0,1,2,3,4.","For fixed k the sequence of S and E steps must be a Dyck path with s steps each, giving Catalan number C_{4-k} possibilities.","There are 2s+1=2(4-k)+1 slots to place k indistinguishable diagonals so the insertion count is binom(8-k,k).","Summing over k gives sum_{k=0}^4 C_{4-k}*binom(8-k,k)=14+35+30+10+1=90."], "answer":"90"}

{"reasoning_steps": ["The diagram marks AB = AC so triangle ABC is isosceles with base BC.", "Thus angle ABC equals angle ACB, and call each x.", "The diagram shows angle ABP = 50° at vertex B.", "Label the unknown angle PBC as y.", "At B the whole angle ABC is the sum ABP + PBC so x = 50° + y.", "Point P lies on side AC in the diagram so angle BCP equals angle BCA, which is x.", "In triangle BPC the three angles at B, C, P are y, x, and 120° respectively as shown.", "The angles in triangle BPC sum to 180°, giving y + x + 120° = 180°.", "Substitute x = 50° + y into the sum to get y + (50° + y) + 120° = 180°.", "This simplifies to 2y + 170° = 180°, so y = 5°.", "Therefore angle PBC = 5°, corresponding to choice A."], "answer": "A"}

{"reasoning_steps":["I see a net of eight equilateral triangles arranged in two rows of four with the top row labeled A, B, C, 5 and the bottom row labeled D, 9, 3, E.","The given face numbers visible are 5, 9, and 3.","The unknowns A, B, C, D, E are to be filled with 2, 4, 6, 7, 8 without repetition as stated.","In an octahedron each vertex is shared by four faces as suggested by the diagram on the right.","The total of all face numbers is 5+9+3+2+4+6+7+8 = 44 based on the visible and available numbers.","Each vertex sum equals half the total face sum, so each vertex sum must be 44/2 = 22.","When folded the four top triangles A, B, C, 5 meet at one vertex based on the net's topology.","When folded the four bottom triangles D, 9, 3, E meet at the opposite vertex based on the net's topology.","The four equatorial vertices correspond to pairs of adjacent top triangles meeting with their underlying bottom triangles, giving equations A+B+D+9=22, B+C+9+3=22, C+5+3+E=22, and 5+A+E+D=22.","These equations simplify to A+B+D=13, B+C=10, C+E=14, and A+D+E=17 as derived from the visible numbers.","The top-apex equation A+B+C+5=22 simplifies to A+B+C=17 based on the visible 5.","Subtracting B+C=10 from A+B+C=17 gives A=7.","Substituting A=7 into A+B+D=13 gives B+D=6.","B+D=6 is attainable by 2+4 only, so B and D are {2,4} and B+D remains 6 regardless of order.","Therefore B+D equals 6."], "answer": "6"}

{"reasoning_steps": ["The left illustration shows a 3-pyramid with three stacked triangular layers containing 1, 3, and 6 balls respectively.", "An n-pyramid stacks triangular layers where the k-th layer contains the triangular number T_k = k(k+1)/2 balls.", "Summing those triangular numbers gives the total balls as the tetrahedral number C(n+2,3).", "Removing all outside balls means removing every ball on any of the four triangular faces of the tetrahedron.", "An interior ball must be at least one ball away from each face which effectively reduces each positional index by 1 and reduces the allowable sum by 3.", "Therefore the remaining balls count equals C(n-1,3) which is the tetrahedral number for n-3 and thus forms an (n-3)-pyramid.", "For n = 8 the remaining figure is an 8-3 = 5-pyramid."], "answer": "C"}

{"reasoning_steps": ["The figure is a 4×4 array of unit squares forming a square grid.", "The corner points of the small squares form a 5×5 lattice of grid vertices, so there are 25 vertices in all.", "A diagonal drawn inside a unit square connects two opposite corners of that square and therefore occupies two of those lattice vertices.", "The condition that no two diagonals have any common point implies in particular that no two diagonals may share a lattice vertex, so the chosen diagonals must be vertex-disjoint.", "Opposite corners of any unit square have the same parity (chessboard) color, so each diagonal uses two vertices of the same color class.", "On a 5×5 checkerboard there are 13 vertices of one color and 12 of the other color.", "Thus at most floor(13/2)+floor(12/2)=6+6=12 vertex-disjoint diagonals can be drawn.", "A drawing that attains 12 is possible (for example one can pair up the vertices into 12 diagonal segments and leave the central vertex unused), so the upper bound 12 is achievable.", "Therefore the maximum possible number of diagonals is 12."], "answer": "12"}

{"reasoning_steps":["The image shows a 3x3 square grid of nine equally spaced black dots.","There are three horizontal rows each containing three dots.","There are three vertical columns each containing three dots.","There are two diagonal lines each containing three dots (the two main diagonals).","Each horizontal row currently contains three collinear dots so each row requires at least one dot removed to avoid a triple.","Removing a single dot lies in exactly one horizontal row so at least three dots must be removed to break all three full rows.","Removing the three dots on the main diagonal (top-left, center, bottom-right) leaves six dots and removes all full horizontal, vertical, and diagonal triples.","Therefore the minimum number of dots to remove so that no three remaining points are collinear is 3."], "answer":"3"}

{"reasoning_steps": ["The grey region is the interior of a triangle shown in the image.","The problem statement gives the area of this triangle as 80 m^2.","The image shows three circles with centers at the triangle's vertices.","The statement says each circle has radius 2 m.","The unshaded corner pieces inside the circles are circular sectors centered at the triangle vertices.","Each sector's central angle equals the triangle's interior angle at that vertex because the sector is bounded by the triangle sides.","The sum of the triangle's interior angles equals pi radians.","The area of a circular sector is 1/2 r^2 theta, making the total removed area 1/2 * r^2 * sum(theta).","Substituting r=2 and sum(theta)=pi gives removed area 1/2 * 4 * pi = 2 pi m^2.","The shaded area equals 80 m^2 minus 2 pi m^2, matching option B."], "answer": "B"}

{"reasoning_steps":["The provided image shows a 4x4 grid gameboard.","There are 4 rows and 4 columns so 8 row-or-column sums must all be different.","Let r_i denote the four row sums.","Let c_j denote the four column sums.","Let T denote the total number of stones.","Each stone contributes to exactly one row and one column so T equals the sum of the row sums and also equals the sum of the column sums.","The eight row-and-column sums are distinct nonnegative integers and their total equals 2T.","The smallest eight distinct nonnegative integers are 0 through 7.","The sum 0+1+2+3+4+5+6+7 equals 28 so T is at least 28/2 = 14.","We must split {0,...,7} into two disjoint 4-element subsets that each sum to 14.","One valid split is rows {0,1,6,7} and columns {2,3,4,5} because each subset sums to 14.","An explicit nonnegative integer 4x4 matrix with those margins is rows (0,0,0,0), (1,0,0,0), (1,3,2,0), (0,0,2,5) which yields column sums (2,3,4,5) and total 14 stones."],"answer":"14"}

{"reasoning_steps": ["The diagram shows square ABCE and AB is labeled with length 1.", "Place coordinates A=(0,0), B=(1,0), C=(1,1), E=(0,1) consistent with the visible square and AB=1.", "Triangle CDE is equilateral built on CE which is the top side of the square.", "The midpoint of CE is (0.5,1).", "D lies above that midpoint by height sqrt(3)/2.", "Therefore D=(0.5,1+sqrt(3)/2).", "BC is vertical with endpoints B=(1,0) and C=(1,1).", "Triangle BCF is equilateral built on BC placing F to the left of BC.", "Therefore F=(1 - sqrt(3)/2,0.5).", "The x-difference FD_x equals 0.5 - (1 - sqrt(3)/2) = (-1+sqrt(3))/2.", "The y-difference FD_y equals (1+sqrt(3)/2) - 0.5 = (1+sqrt(3))/2.", "FD^2 equals FD_x^2 + FD_y^2 which equals 2.", "Thus FD equals sqrt(2)."], "answer": "A"}

{"reasoning_steps":["The diagram shows a 3x3 grid of numbered circular nodes with A left of the bottom-left node and B right of the top-right node.","Arrows in the diagram point right along each row and point upward in each column as visible.","The bottom row left-to-right shows values 1, 2, 1 as read from the circles.","The middle row left-to-right shows values 2, 3, 2 as read from the circles.","The top row left-to-right shows values 1, 2, 1 as read from the circles.","The route must start at A then visit the bottom-left node marked 1 as shown.","To reach the top-right node before B one must make exactly two right moves and exactly two up moves as implied by the grid positions.","There are 6 directed paths from A to B corresponding to the different orders of two ups and two rights (C(4,2)=6).","The path sequence U U R R visits nodes with values 1,2,1,2,1 and sums to 7.","The path sequences U R U R, U R R U, R U U R, and R U R U each visit nodes with values 1,2,3,2,1 and sum to 9.","The path sequence R R U U visits nodes with values 1,2,1,2,1 and sums to 7.","The distinct sums visible from these paths are 7 and 9 which yields two different results."], "answer":"2"}
