{"reasoning_steps": ["The plot's horizontal axis is labeled \"Zeit\" (time) and the vertical axis is labeled \"Strecke\" (distance).", "Five points are plotted and labeled Anja, Bernd, Chris, Doris, and Ernst.", "Average speed corresponds to distance divided by time and therefore to the slope of the line from the origin through each point.", "Chris's point is the highest in distance and is relatively leftward in time compared with the others.", "Anja's point is far right and low, indicating a long time and a small distance.", "Ernst's point is right of center with moderate distance and thus a shallower slope than Chris.", "Doris and Bernd have lower distances than Chris and similar or slightly smaller times than Chris.", "Visually, Chris's origin-to-point slope is the steepest among the five points."], "answer": "C"}

{"reasoning_steps": ["The left image shows a triangle with a dashed line indicating a fold.", "The right image shows the triangle after folding with two grey triangular regions and a central overlapped region.", "Let T denote the area of the original triangle and O denote the overlapped area after folding.", "The two parts of the triangle partition area so their sum equals T.", "The area of the resulting figure after folding equals T minus O because the overlap is counted once.", "The problem states T equals 1.5 times the area of the resulting figure, so T = 1.5*(T - O).", "Solving that equation gives O = (1/3)T.", "The two grey regions are the non-overlapped parts from each side, so their total area equals T - 2O.", "Substituting O = (1/3)T gives the grey total equal to (1/3)T.", "The problem gives the grey total as 1, so (1/3)T = 1 and therefore T = 3."], "answer": "3"}

{"reasoning_steps":["The image shows two rows of interconnected shopping trolleys.","The problem states the first row is 2.9 m long and consists of 10 trolleys.","The problem states the second row is 4.9 m long and consists of 20 trolleys.","Interconnected trolleys imply a constant overlap between adjacent trolleys.","Let x denote the length of one trolley and let d denote the overlap per connection.","For 10 trolleys the total length equals 10x - 9d and this equals 2.9 m.","For 20 trolleys the total length equals 20x - 19d and this equals 4.9 m.","Subtracting the first equation from the second gives 2.0 m = 10(x - d).","Hence x - d = 0.2 m.","Plugging x - d = 0.2 m into 2.9 = 10x - 9d yields x = 1.1 m.","The correct multiple-choice option is C."], "answer":"C"}

{"reasoning_steps":["The figure shows a triangle with lines drawn parallel to the base that divide the two non-base sides into 10 equal parts.","Those parallel lines produce 10 horizontal strips counted from the apex (top) down to the base.","The shading alternates and includes the top small triangle and every other strip below it, i.e., strips numbered 1, 3, 5, 7, 9 from the apex.","By similarity the area from the apex down to the line at i/10 of the side equals (i/10)^2 of the whole triangle.","Hence the area of the ith strip equals (i/10)^2 - ((i-1)/10)^2 of the whole triangle.","The shaded fraction therefore equals the sum for i = 1,3,5,7,9 of (i/10)^2 - ((i-1)/10)^2.","Each such strip fraction simplifies to (2i-1)/100, so the shaded total is (1+5+9+13+17)/100 = 45/100 = 45%."],"answer":"C"}

{"reasoning_steps": ["The diagram shows an angle with vertex O and the interior angle alpha marked as 7°.", "The segments OA1, A1A2, A2A3, ... are indicated as all equal in length.", "The points A1, A2, A3, ... lie alternately on the two sides of the angle as the broken line zigzags downward.", "Reflecting the angle across its sides unfolds the zigzag into a single straight segment in the reflected plane.", "After n segments the corresponding straight line in the unfolded plane subtends an angle of n*alpha with the original side and this angle must be less than 180° to prevent intersections when folded back.", "Hence the number n of segments satisfies n*alpha < 180°, so n ≤ floor(180°/alpha).", "Substituting alpha = 7° gives n ≤ floor(180°/7°) = floor(25.714...) = 25.", "Therefore the maximum number of nonintersecting equal segments is 25."], "answer": "25"}

{"reasoning_steps": ["The image shows an alternating sequence of black and white vertical stripes starting and ending with black.", "Each stripe width is either 1 or 2 and the total width is 12.", "Let n be the number of stripes.", "Because colors alternate and the first and last are black, n must be odd.", "The n stripe widths are 1 or 2 and they sum to 12.", "Let t be the number of stripes of width 2 so n + t = 12.", "From n + t = 12 and 0 ≤ t ≤ n it follows that 6 ≤ n ≤ 12.", "The odd values of n in that range are 7, 9, and 11.", "For n = 7 we must have t = 5 and there are C(7,5) = 21 choices for positions of the 2s.", "For n = 9 we must have t = 3 and there are C(9,3) = 84 choices for positions of the 2s.", "For n = 11 we must have t = 1 and there are C(11,1) = 11 choices for positions of the 2s.", "Summing the counts gives 21 + 84 + 11 = 116 possible barcodes."], "answer": "116"}

{"reasoning_steps": ["The central polygon is a regular hexagon with side length 1 as given.", "There are six squares attached, one to each side of the hexagon as shown.", "Each attached square has side length 1 because it shares a side with the hexagon.", "There are six equilateral triangles located at the hexagon vertices between adjacent squares as shown.", "Each equilateral triangle has side length 1 because it uses edges coinciding with the hexagon vertex and square edges of length 1.", "Each square has its hexagon-attached side and its two sides shared with a triangle as interior edges not on the outer boundary.", "Each square therefore contributes exactly one outer side of length 1 to the perimeter.", "Each triangle shares two sides with adjacent squares and therefore contributes exactly its base of length 1 to the outer perimeter.", "The outer perimeter thus consists of 6 outer square sides and 6 triangle bases, each of length 1.", "The total perimeter is 6*1 + 6*1 = 12."], "answer": "12"}

{"reasoning_steps":["Given that opposite faces on each die sum to 7.","Given that each pair of touching faces between adjacent dice sum to 5.","The visible pip on the right face of the bottom die indicates that right face equals 1.","Let t1, t2, t3 denote the top-face values of the top, middle, and bottom dice respectively.","For the top die the bottom face equals 7 - t1.","The contact of top and middle dice gives (7 - t1) + t2 = 5.","From that equation t2 = t1 - 2.","For the middle die the bottom face equals 7 - t2.","The contact of middle and bottom dice gives (7 - t2) + t3 = 5.","From that equation t3 = t2 - 2.","Combining gives t3 = t1 - 4.","Top-face values must be integers from 1 to 6 so t1 >= 5 and thus t1 is 5 or 6.","If t1 = 5 then t3 = 1.","A single die cannot have the same number on two different faces so t1 ≠ 5.","Thus t1 = 6."],"answer":"6"}

{"reasoning_steps":["The side view of the cone is given as an equilateral triangle so the apex angle of the cone is 60°.","Therefore the semi-vertical angle between the cone axis and a side is 30°.","Let the hole depth from rim to apex be x and the marble radius be r = 15 (given).","The marble's center is r below the rim so its distance from the apex is x - r.","The perpendicular distance from the axis to a side at height y from the apex equals y·sin30° = y/2 because the side makes 30° with the axis.","Tangency of the sphere to the cone side gives r = (x - r)/2.","Solving r = (x - r)/2 with r = 15 yields x - r = 30 and hence x = 45."],"answer":"45"}

{"reasoning_steps": ["The image shows a 4x4 grid with numbers alongside the rows and below the columns.","The numbers to the right of the rows read from top to bottom as \"2 0 1 1\".","The numbers below the columns read from left to right as \"2 0 1 1\".","Therefore the required row sums are [2,0,1,1] and the required column sums are [2,0,1,1].","The row with sum 0 must be entirely zeros.","The column with sum 0 must be entirely zeros.","Removing that zero row and zero column leaves a 3x3 subgrid with row sums [2,1,1] and column sums [2,1,1].","Count 3x3 binary matrices by choosing which two columns contain the two ones in the first (sum-2) row.","If the first row has ones in columns (1,2) then the remaining rows have 2 completions.","If the first row has ones in columns (1,3) then the remaining rows have 2 completions.","If the first row has ones in columns (2,3) then the remaining rows have 1 completion.","Summing completions gives 5 possible fillings for the 3x3 subgrid.","The zero row and zero column are fixed so there are 5 possible colourings of the full 4x4 grid."], "answer": "5"}

{"reasoning_steps": ["The top-left cell shows 1.", "The top-right cell shows 0.", "The center cell shows 2.", "The bottom-left cell shows 4.", "The bottom-right cell shows 3.", "Let a denote cell (1,2), b denote cell (2,1), c denote cell (2,3), and d denote cell (3,2).", "The top-left 2x2 sub-table gives a + b + 1 + 2 = 10.", "The top-right 2x2 sub-table gives a + c + 0 + 2 = 10.", "The bottom-left 2x2 sub-table gives b + d + 2 + 4 = 10.", "The bottom-right 2x2 sub-table gives c + d + 2 + 3 = 10.", "From the first equation a + b = 7.", "From the fourth equation c + d = 5.", "Therefore a + b + c + d = 7 + 5 = 12."], "answer": "12"}

{"reasoning_steps":["The figure shows triangle W X Y with Z on segment X Y and T on segment W Z.","At vertex W the rays W X, W T and W Y are visible and the two labelled angles α1 and α2 partition the triangle vertex angle at W.","At vertex X the rays X W, X T and X Y are visible and the two labelled angles α3 and α4 partition the triangle vertex angle at X.","At vertex Y the single labelled angle is α7 and it equals the triangle vertex angle at Y.","Hence the three triangle vertex angles are α1+α2, α3+α4 and α7, giving at most three independent measures coming from the big triangle vertices.","The intersection T of lines W Z and T X shows two interior angles α8 and α9 at T that in general are independent of the three vertex-angle partitions.","The point Z on X Y also yields local angles (α5 and α6) that are not simply equal to the three triangle vertex angles in general.","Putting these visible relations together shows there must generally be at least five distinct angle measures among the nine labelled angles."],"answer":"5"}

{"reasoning_steps": ["The diagram shows two circles intersecting at X and Y with XY the diameter of the small circle.", "Point S is labeled as the centre of the large circle and lies on the small circle as stated.", "Let R denote the small circle radius and r denote the large circle radius as given.", "The midpoint M of XY is the small circle centre and satisfies MX = R.", "For the large circle the perpendicular from its centre S to chord XY passes through M so SM is perpendicular to XY.", "Triangle SMX is right-angled at M with legs SM = R and MX = R.", "By the Pythagorean theorem SX = r = R * sqrt(2) so R = r / sqrt(2).", "The small circle area is pi*R^2 = pi*(r^2/2) = (pi/2) r^2.", "In the overlap formula the first arccos argument equals 1/sqrt(2) so its arccos is pi/4.", "In the overlap formula the second arccos argument equals 0 so its arccos is pi/2.", "The two sector terms sum to r^2*(pi/4) + (r^2/2)*(pi/2) = r^2*(pi/2).", "The radical term inside the overlap formula simplifies to r^4 so its square root is r^2 and half of that is (1/2) r^2.", "Thus the intersection (overlap) area equals r^2*(pi/2) - (1/2) r^2.", "The grey region equals small area minus overlap = (pi/2) r^2 - (r^2*(pi/2) - (1/2) r^2) = (1/2) r^2.", "The area equals (1/2) r^2 which corresponds to choice C."], "answer": "C"}

{"reasoning_steps": ["The diagram shows an isosceles triangle with M and N marked as midpoints of the equal sides.", "Segments BN and CM cross at a point P and partition the triangle into three regions labeled 3, 3, and 6 and a top quadrilateral labeled ?.", "By symmetry the intersection P lies on the altitude from the apex and the cevians meet at P two-thirds of the way from each base vertex toward the opposite midpoint (t = 2/3), placing P at height h/3.", "Hence the bottom triangle (BPC) has height h/3 and base BC, so its area is one third of the whole triangle's area.", "Since the bottom region is labeled 6 the whole triangle area is 3 * 6 = 18.", "Subtracting the known interior areas 3 + 3 + 6 = 12 from the total 18 gives the top quadrilateral area 6."], "answer": "6"}

{"reasoning_steps": ["AB lies on the vertical line g as shown.", "ABCD is drawn as a square with side length 4 cm as given.", "The area of quadrilateral ABCD is 4*4 = 16 cm^2.", "CD is the left vertical side of the square and has length 4 cm as shown.", "Triangle ECD has base CD so its area equals one half times CD times the perpendicular distance from E to line CD.", "The perpendicular distance from E to line CD equals the perpendicular distance from E to line g minus 4 cm because CD is 4 cm left of g in the figure.", "Denote by x the perpendicular distance from E to line g.", "The area of triangle ECD therefore equals 2*(x-4) cm^2 and setting 2*(x-4)=16 gives x=12 cm."], "answer": "C"}

{"reasoning_steps": ["The diagram shows a right triangle with base labeled 12, vertical leg labeled 5, and hypotenuse labeled 13.", "The semicircle's diameter lies on the base and its rightmost diameter endpoint coincides with the triangle's right vertex at the vertical leg.", "If the full circle's center is at (a,0) on the base, the right endpoint condition gives a + r = 12.", "The hypotenuse through (0,0) and (12,5) has equation y = (5/12)x.", "The perpendicular distance from (a,0) to the line y = (5/12)x equals 5a/13 and must equal r for tangency.", "Solving a + r = 12 with r = 5a/13 gives a = 26/3 and r = 10/3.", "Therefore the semicircle radius is 10/3 corresponding to choice 'B'."], "answer": "B"}

{"reasoning_steps": ["The image shows a 3x4 grid with top row [2, 4, blank, 2], middle row [blank, 3, 3, blank], and bottom row [6, blank, 1, grey].", "Let the top-row blank be x, the middle-left blank be y, the middle-right blank be z, the bottom-middle blank be w, and the grey square be g.", "Let every row sum equal R and every column sum equal C.", "Row 1 gives 2+4+x+2 = 8+x = R.", "Row 2 gives y+3+3+z = y+z+6 = R.", "Row 3 gives 6+w+1+g = 7+w+g = R.", "Column 1 gives 2+y+6 = y+8 = C.", "Column 2 gives 4+3+w = 7+w = C.", "Column 3 gives x+3+1 = x+4 = C.", "Column 4 gives 2+z+g = z+g+2 = C.", "Equating row and column expressions for x gives R = C+4.", "The global relation 3R = 4C thus yields C = 12 and R = 16.", "From C = 12 we get x = 8, y = 4, and w = 5 from the column equations.", "From R = 16 and y = 4 we get z = 6 from y+z+6 = R.", "From C = 12 and z = 6 we get g = 4 from z+g+2 = C.", "Therefore the grey square contains the number 4."], "answer": "4"}

{"reasoning_steps": ["The diagram labels rectangle ABCD with A top-left, B bottom-left, C bottom-right, and D top-right.", "The rectangle dimensions are 16 cm by 4 cm as given.", "I place B at (0,0) and A at (0,4) to match the left-side height in the figure.", "From the width 16, C is at (16,0) and D is at (16,4).", "The fold maps corner C to corner A as stated in the problem.", "The crease is the perpendicular bisector of AC.", "The midpoint of AC is (8,2).", "The slope of AC is -1/4 based on its coordinates.", "The crease is perpendicular to AC so its slope is 4.", "The crease meets the top edge y=4 at M with x=8.5 giving M(17/2,4).", "The crease meets the bottom edge y=0 at N with x=7.5 giving N(15/2,0).", "Point D is (16,4).", "Reflecting D across the crease produces D' at (32/17,128/17).", "The pentagon ABNMD' has vertices A(0,4), B(0,0), N(15/2,0), M(17/2,4), and D'(32/17,128/17).", "Applying the shoelace formula to those vertices gives area 799/17 cm^2.", "799/17 simplifies to 47 cm^2."], "answer": "D"}

{"reasoning_steps": ["Each square is divided visually into a 3x3 grid of equal small squares as shown by the uniform band thicknesses.", "Take the small-square side as 1 so the plain paper square side is 3 and its perimeter is 12.", "Figure 1 is an L occupying the left column and bottom row for 5 small squares.", "A polyomino perimeter equals 4*(# squares) - 2*(# adjacent shared edges).", "Figure 1 has 5 squares and 4 adjacent shared edges so its perimeter is 4*5-2*4 = 12, matching the paper.", "Figure 2 is an H occupying two columns and the middle row for 7 small squares.", "Figure 2 has 7 squares and 6 adjacent edges so its perimeter is 4*7-2*6 = 16, not matching.", "Figure 3 is a U occupying both columns and the bottom row for 7 small squares.", "Figure 3 has 7 squares and 6 adjacent edges so its perimeter is 16, not matching.", "Figure 4 is a stair/mirrored-L shape occupying 5 small squares.", "Figure 4 has 5 squares and 4 adjacent edges so its perimeter is 12, matching.", "Figure 5 is a T (top row plus middle column) occupying 5 small squares.", "Figure 5 has 5 squares and 4 adjacent edges so its perimeter is 12, matching.", "Figure 6 is a plus (middle row and middle column) occupying 5 small squares.", "Figure 6 has 5 squares and 4 adjacent edges so its perimeter is 12, matching."], "answer": "4"}

{"reasoning_steps":["The diagram shows a regular hexagon.","The labels indicate A and B are opposite vertices.","The labels indicate C and D are midpoints of two opposite sides.","Let the hexagon side length be s.","In a regular hexagon the circumradius equals the side length.","Thus AB, the distance between opposite vertices, equals 2s.","The midpoint of a side lies at distance s*cos(30°) = s*√3/2 from the center.","Thus CD, the distance between opposite midpoints, equals 2*(s*√3/2) = s√3.","The area of a regular hexagon equals (3√3/2) s^2.","Setting (3√3/2) s^2 = 60 gives s^2 = 40/√3.","Therefore AB*CD = (2s)*(s√3) = 2 s^2 √3 = 80."],"answer":"80"}

{"reasoning_steps": ["Points A and B are endpoints of the horizontal segment AB with C above AB and D below AB as shown.", "Triangle ABC is marked with angles 60° at C and 61° at B.", "Angle A of triangle ABC is 59°.", "Triangle ABD is marked with angles 59° at D and 60° at A.", "Angle B of triangle ABD is 61°.", "By the law of sines in triangle ABC, AC/sin61° = AB/sin60° = BC/sin59°.", "By the law of sines in triangle ABD, AD/sin61° = BD/sin60° = AB/sin59°.", "Numerically sin59°≈0.857167, sin60°=0.866025, and sin61°≈0.874618.", "Setting AB=1 gives AC≈sin61°/sin60°≈1.00984.", "Setting AB=1 gives BC≈sin59°/sin60°≈0.98980.", "Setting AB=1 gives AD≈sin61°/sin59°≈1.01994.", "Setting AB=1 gives BD≈sin60°/sin59°≈1.01032.", "Comparing AB=1, AC≈1.00984, BC≈0.98980, AD≈1.01994, and BD≈1.01032 shows AD is the longest segment."], "answer": "A"}

{"reasoning_steps": ["The front face shows \"35\".", "The top face shows \"18\".", "The right face shows \"14\".", "The three opposite faces are stated to be prime numbers.", "The sums of numbers on opposite faces are equal.", "Call the common total S.", "Let p1 be the prime opposite 35.", "Let p2 be the prime opposite 18.", "Let p3 be the prime opposite 14.", "Then S = 35 + p1 = 18 + p2 = 14 + p3.", "From these equalities p2 = p1 + 17.", "From these equalities p3 = p1 + 21.", "Try the smallest prime p1 = 2.", "Then p2 = 19.", "Then p3 = 23.", "Both 19 and 23 are primes.", "Therefore S = 35 + 2 = 37.", "Hence the number opposite 14 is 23."], "answer": "23"}

{"reasoning_steps": ["The diagram shows a square ABCD with area 80.", "Let the side length be s so s^2 = 80.", "Points E, F, G, H lie on sides AB, BC, CD, DA respectively as labeled in the figure.", "The problem gives AE = BF = CG = DH and AE = 3·EB, so AE = 3(s - AE) and hence AE = 3s/4.", "Therefore AE = BF = CG = DH = 3s/4 and the remaining segments EB = FC = DG = HA = s/4.", "Place coordinates A=(0,s), B=(s,s), C=(s,0), D=(0,0) consistent with the figure orientation.", "Then E=(3s/4,s), F=(s,s/4), G=(s/4,0), H=(0,3s/4) by measuring along the sides.", "The drawn diagonals EG and HF intersect and solving their parametric equations gives intersection P=(s/2,s/2) at the square center.", "Compute area of triangle EHP by 1/2|det(E-P,H-P)| which evaluates to s^2·5/32.", "By symmetry triangle PFG has the same area so the shaded total area is 2·(5/32 s^2) = 5/16 s^2.", "Substituting s^2 = 80 gives shaded area = 5/16·80 = 25."], "answer": "25"}

{"reasoning_steps":["The diagram shows three overlapping circles forming seven internal zones.","The left pairwise-overlap zone is labeled \"1\".","The right pairwise-overlap zone is labeled \"2\".","The central triple-overlap zone is labeled \"?\".","Call the single-circle-only zones A (left), B (top), C (right), call AB=1, BC=2, AC=x, and call the center T.","By adjacency each pairwise zone is adjacent to its two corresponding single-only zones and to the central triple zone.","Therefore 1 = AB = A + B + T.","Therefore 2 = BC = B + C + T.","Therefore x = AC = A + C + T.","By adjacency each single-only zone equals the sum of its two adjacent pairwise zones.","Hence A = AB + AC.","Hence B = AB + BC.","Hence C = AC + BC.","Substituting AB=1 and BC=2 gives A = 1 + x, B = 3, and C = x + 2.","Substituting A and B into 1 = A + B + T yields 1 = (1 + x) + 3 + T and hence x + T = -3.","Also T = AB + BC + AC = 1 + 2 + x = 3 + x.","Combining x + T = -3 and T = 3 + x gives 2x + 3 = -3.","Solving gives x = -3.","Then T = 3 + x = 0.","Therefore the number in the inner area equals 0."],"answer":"0"}

{"reasoning_steps": ["Left figure shows triangle ABC with a line through X parallel to AC separating a small unshaded triangle at the top and a shaded trapezoid at the bottom.", "Right figure shows triangle ABC with a line through Y parallel to AC separating a small shaded triangle at the top and an unshaded trapezoid at the bottom.", "BX:XA = 4:1 implies BX/BA = 4/(4+1) = 4/5.", "Similar triangles give area of the small top triangle in the left figure as (BX/BA)^2 = (4/5)^2 = 16/25 of the whole triangle.", "Shaded trapezoid area in the left figure equals whole area minus top small triangle area = 1 - 16/25 = 9/25 of the whole triangle.", "The shaded top triangle in the right figure therefore equals 9/25 of the whole triangle by the problem statement that the grey areas are equal.", "The shaded top triangle area fraction in the right figure equals (BY/BA)^2, so (BY/BA)^2 = 9/25 and BY/BA = 3/5.", "BY:YA therefore equals 3:2."], "answer": "D"}

{"reasoning_steps": ["Each side of the outer triangle is labeled with segments 1, 3, 1 so the full side length is 5 units by visible labels.", "The points that cut off the grey region lie at distance 1 from each vertex, which is 1/5 of each side by the labels.", "The segment joining the two points at distance 1 from a vertex is parallel to the opposite side and therefore forms a smaller triangle similar to the big triangle as suggested by the symmetry and parallelism.", "The linear scale factor of each small corner triangle relative to the big triangle is 1/5 as seen from the 1 versus 5 side partition.", "The area scale factor is the square of the linear scale factor, so each corner triangle has area 1/25 of the big triangle.", "Three congruent corner triangles are removed, so the removed area is 3*(1/25)=3/25 of the whole triangle.", "The grey area fraction is 1-3/25 = 22/25, which equals 0.88 or 88% as a percent."], "answer": "C"}

{"reasoning_steps":["The image shows a 3x3 grid with top-left cell 20 and top-middle cell 1.","The nine numbers used are 1,2,4,5,10,20,25,50,100 as stated.","Each row, column, and diagonal must have the same product P.","The product of all nine numbers is 1*2*4*5*10*20*25*50*100 = 10^9.","The product of the three row-products equals the total product, so P^3 = 10^9 and P = 1000.","From the top row 20*1*top-right = 1000 so top-right = 50.","From the right column 50 * middle-right * bottom-right = 1000 so middle-right * bottom-right = 20.","From the left column 20 * middle-left * bottom-left = 1000 so middle-left * bottom-left = 50.","Using these relations with the remaining numbers gives center=10, middle-left=25, bottom-left=2, bottom-right=5, and middle-right = 4."],"answer":"4"}

{"reasoning_steps":["The image shows a 3×3 square grid of nine cells.","The problem requires every row, every column and both main diagonals to each contain three cells with three different colours.","Using only 2 colours is impossible because a length-3 row would force a repeated colour.","With 3 colours every row and every column must be a permutation of the three colours.","Fixing the first row as (1,2,3) and the second row as either (2,3,1) or (3,1,2) forces the third row to be (3,1,2) or (2,3,1) respectively.","Each of those two Latin squares has one diagonal constant so one diagonal fails to have three different colours.","Assume 4 colours and let the main diagonal entries be a, b, c distinct.","The cell at (1,3) cannot equal a (same row), cannot equal b (diagonal must differ) and cannot equal c (same column) so it must be the unique fourth colour.","By the same reasoning the cell at (3,1) must also be that unique fourth colour.","Thus the two off-diagonal cells coincide and the anti-diagonal cannot have three different colours, so 4 colours are insufficient.","Label five colours 1,2,3,4,5 and colour the grid row-wise as [1,3,4; 4,2,1; 5,1,3].","Each row in that colouring contains three distinct colours.","Each column in that colouring contains three distinct colours.","The two main diagonals contain (1,2,3) and (4,2,5) which are each three distinct colours.","Therefore 5 colours suffice and no smaller number works."], "answer": "5"}

{"reasoning_steps":["The diagram shows the plant makes exactly five complete twists around the post.","The diagram marks the vertical rise of the helix as 1 m.","The problem statement gives the post circumference as 15 cm.","Convert the circumference to meters as 0.15 m.","The vertical rise per turn is 1 m divided by 5 which equals 0.2 m.","The length of one helical turn equals sqrt((vertical rise per turn)^2 + (circumference)^2) which equals sqrt(0.2^2 + 0.15^2).","The per-turn length computes to sqrt(0.04 + 0.0225) = sqrt(0.0625) = 0.25 m.","The total plant length equals 5 times 0.25 m which equals 1.25 m.","The matching multiple-choice option is C which is 1.25 m."],"answer":"C"}

{"reasoning_steps":["AB and CD are the parallel bases of the trapezium with AB=50 and CD=20 as given.","Let the distance between the bases (height) be h.","Place A at (0,0) and B at (50,0) so AB lies on the x-axis.","Let D be at (x0,h) and C at (x0+20,h) for some x0, so CD has length 20 at height h.","Let E lie on AB with coordinate (x_E,0) so AE = x_E.","The area of the trapezium is (AB+CD)/2 * h = (50+20)/2 * h = 35h.","Half the trapezium area is 17.5h due to DE dividing the trapezium into two equal-area parts.","The region on the left is triangle ADE with area (1/2)*AE*h = (1/2)*x_E*h.","Equating areas gives (1/2)*x_E*h = 17.5h, cancelling h yields x_E = 35, so AE = 35."],"answer":"35"}

{"reasoning_steps": ["The problem and diagram show an equilateral triangle with perpendiculars drawn from each side midpoint to the other two sides.", "Choose coordinates with side length 2 and height √3 so A=(0,√3), B=(-1,0), C=(1,0) for convenience.", "The side midpoints are M_a=(0,0), M_b=(1/2,√3/2), and M_c=(-1/2,√3/2) which match the dots on the sides in the figure.", "The perpendicular lines from M_a have equations y=±x/√3, the perpendiculars from M_b are x=1/2 and y=-x/√3+2/√3, and the perpendiculars from M_c are x=-1/2 and y=x/√3+2/√3 by slope calculations.", "The six intersection points of those lines inside the triangle are (0,0), (±1/2,√3/6), and (0,2/√3) which correspond to the three midpoints and three interior points visible in the diagram.", "The shaded hexagon therefore has vertices in cyclic order (0,2/√3), (1/2,√3/2), (1/2,√3/6), (0,0), (-1/2,√3/6), (-1/2,√3/2) as seen from the picture and coordinate calculations.", "Using the shoelace formula on those exact coordinates yields hexagon area √3/6 + 1/√3 which simplifies to √3/2.", "The total triangle area for side length 2 is √3, so the hexagon area is exactly half of the triangle area by division.", "Given the triangle area is 1 the hexagon area is 1/2."], "answer": "D"}

{"reasoning_steps": ["The diagram shows three wheels A, B, C connected by belts that rotate without sliding.", "No slipping implies equal linear belt travel so rotation_count times circumference is equal for two contacting wheels.", "The problem states that when B rotates 4 times, A rotates 5 times.", "Therefore 4 * C_B = 5 * C_A.", "The problem also states that when B rotates 6 times, C rotates 7 times.", "Therefore 6 * C_B = 7 * C_C.", "The circumference of C is given as 30 cm.", "From 6 * C_B = 7 * 30 we get C_B = 35 cm.", "From 4 * 35 = 5 * C_A we get C_A = 28 cm.", "The correct answer choice is B."], "answer": "B"}

{"reasoning_steps": ["The 3x3 diagram shows 3 in the top-left corner, 1 in the top-right corner, 2 in the bottom-left corner, and ? in the bottom-right corner.", "Label the remaining cells as top-middle = x, middle-left = a, center = b, middle-right = c, and bottom-middle = y.", "The sum of the top-left 2x2 square is 3 + x + a + b.", "The sum of the top-right 2x2 square is x + 1 + b + c.", "Equal sums for those two 2x2 squares give 3 + x + a + b = x + 1 + b + c, which implies a - c = -2.", "The sum of the bottom-left 2x2 square is a + b + 2 + y.", "The sum of the bottom-right 2x2 square is b + c + y + ?.", "Equal sums for those two 2x2 squares give a + b + 2 + y = b + c + y + ?, which simplifies to a - c + 2 - ? = 0.", "Substituting a - c = -2 into a - c + 2 - ? = 0 gives -2 + 2 - ? = 0, which implies ? = 0."], "answer": "0"}

{"reasoning_steps": ["I count 6 rows in the triangular wall from the visible layers of bricks.", "The base row therefore has 6 tiles and the total number of tiles is 6+5+4+3+2+1 = 21.", "The condition that each tile equals the sum of the two tiles directly below implies the parity of any tile equals the sum mod 2 of the two tiles below, so the base parities determine all parities.", "Pascal's triangle mod 2 gives the coefficient rows used to propagate base parities upward, and for r=0..5 these rows are r0=[1], r1=[1,1], r2=[1,0,1], r3=[1,1,1,1], r4=[1,0,0,0,1], r5=[1,1,0,0,1,1] by inspection.", "I form the 6 column contribution patterns (one for each base position) by sliding these mod-2 rows up the triangle to see how a single odd base tile affects all entries.", "I tested combinations of base parities by XORing those column patterns to count resulting odd tiles in the whole wall.", "The base parity vector b=(1,0,1,1,0,1) (odd, even, odd, odd, even, odd on the 6 base tiles) yields exactly 15 odd tiles when the column patterns are XORed.", "It is impossible for all 21 tiles to be odd because the mod-2 equations b0+b4=1 and b1+b5=1 together imply b0+b1+b4+b5=0, contradicting the top-row requirement b0+b1+b4+b5=1, so 21 cannot be achieved.", "After checking combinations and using the mod-2 propagation, no base parity vector produces more than 15 odd tiles."], "answer": "15"}

{"reasoning_steps": ["The six masses given are 101, 102, 103, 104, 105, and 106 grams.", "There are C(6,3)=20 equally likely ways to place three weights on the right tray.", "The total mass is 621 grams so the right tray is heavier exactly when its sum is at least 311 grams.", "If 106 g is on the right then the other two must sum to at least 205 grams and among pairs from 101–105 eight pairs meet this requirement.", "Thus eight distributions have 106 g on the right and make the right tray heavier.", "Among triples without 106 g, exactly two triples (105+104+103 and 105+104+102) have sum at least 311 grams.", "Therefore ten distributions make the right tray heavier in total.", "Hence the conditional probability that 106 g is on the right given the right tray is heavier is 8/10 = 80%."], "answer": "B"}

{"reasoning_steps":["The diagram shows A and M on a horizontal line with P further left on that line and B on the circle above the line.","MB is a radius of the circle, so denote MB = r and note r is a whole number.","PA is a segment on the same line with length a whole number, denote PA = d.","The diagram and text state PB is tangent at B, so PB is perpendicular to MB and PB = PA + 6 = d + 6.","For an external point P the tangent length squared equals PM^2 - r^2, so (d+6)^2 = PM^2 - r^2.","The points are collinear in order P-A-M so PM = PA + AM = d + r.","Substituting gives (d+6)^2 = (d + r)^2 - r^2 = d^2 + 2dr, which simplifies to d(r - 6) = 18.","Since d and r are positive integers, d must be a positive divisor of 18, giving six possibilities d in {1,2,3,6,9,18}.","Each divisor yields an integer r = 6 + 18/d and thus six possible values for MB."],"answer":"6"}

{"reasoning_steps":["The diagram is a directed network from A (filled dot at the lower-left) to B (filled dot at the upper-right) with a central node between them.","The left cluster displays three nodes (A bottom, an upper-left open node, and a middle-left open node) arranged in a small triangle next to the center.","Arrowheads show directed edges A->upper-left, A->middle-left, and A->center.","Arrowheads also show directed edges upper-left->middle-left, upper-left->center, and middle-left->center into the center node.","Therefore the distinct directed paths from A to the center are A->center, A->middle-left->center, A->upper-left->center, and A->upper-left->middle-left->center, totaling 4 ways.","The right cluster visibly mirrors the left cluster around the central node.","The directed arrows on the right cluster therefore create the same count of directed paths from the center to B as exist from A to the center.","By symmetry there are 4 distinct directed ways to go from the center to B.","Combining any of the 4 ways to reach the center with any of the 4 ways from the center to B yields 4 × 4 = 16 distinct A→B paths."], "answer":"16"}

{"reasoning_steps": ["The square has side length 4 as stated.", "The diagram shows two congruent semicircles on each side spanning the full side.", "Thus each semicircle has diameter 2 and radius 1.", "Placing the square with corners at (0,0) and (4,4) gives semicircle centers at (1,0),(3,0),(0,1),(0,3),(4,1),(4,3),(1,4),(3,4).", "Each semicircle has area π/2.", "The sum of the eight semicircle areas is 8·(π/2) = 4π.", "Centers separated by distance 2 are tangent with no overlap and centers separated by distance 4 are disjoint, so only the four corner-adjacent center pairs are at distance √2 and overlap.", "The intersection area of two unit circles with center distance √2 equals 2·arccos(√2/2) - (√2/2)·√(4-2) which simplifies to π/2 - 1.", "There are four such overlapping pairs so the total overlap area to subtract is 4·(π/2 - 1).", "The union area of all semicircles inside the square is 4π - 4·(π/2 - 1) = 2π + 4.", "The white central area equals the square area 16 minus that union area, giving 16 - (2π + 4) = 12 - 2π."], "answer": "12 - 2π"}

{"reasoning_steps": ["The annulus has inner radius 1 and outer radius 9.", "Let s be the small circle radius and d be its center distance from the annulus center.", "Tangency to the inner circle gives d = 1 + s.", "Tangency to the outer circle gives d = 9 - s.", "Equating the two expressions gives s = 4.", "Substituting gives d = 5.", "All centers of such circles lie on the circle of radius 5 centered at the origin.", "Two such circles do not overlap only if the distance between their centers is at least 8.", "For a central angle theta the distance between centers is 2*5*sin(theta/2).", "The nonoverlap condition becomes 2*5*sin(theta/2) >= 8.", "Hence sin(theta/2) >= 0.8 and theta >= 2*arcsin(0.8).", "The largest integer number of circles is floor(360 degrees / 106.2602048 degrees) = 3."], "answer": "3"}

{"reasoning_steps": ["The figure is an 18-sided polygon with vertex A marked at the top.", "The problem states each vertex value equals the sum of the two adjacent vertex values, which is visible in the text.", "Rearranging that relation gives the linear recurrence x_{n+1}=x_n-x_{n-1}.", "The recurrence has characteristic roots e^{±iπ/3} so the sequence is periodic with period 6 and x_{n+6}=x_n.", "Label the top vertex A as x0=a and the next clockwise vertex as x1=b, which matches the visible clockwise orientation.", "The period-6 pattern starting at x0 is x0=a, x1=b, x2=b-a, x3=-a, x4=-b, x5=a-b.", "Counting clockwise from A in the image shows the vertex labeled \"18\" is eight steps from A, i.e., it is x8.", "Counting clockwise from A in the image shows the vertex labeled \"20\" is ten steps from A, i.e., it is x10.", "By periodicity x8=x2=b-a and x10=x4=-b.", "The picture gives x8=18 and x10=20 as visible text.", "From x10=-b=20 we get b=-20.", "From x8=b-a=18 we get -20-a=18 and hence a=-38.", "Therefore the number written at vertex A is -38."], "answer": "-38"}

{"reasoning_steps": ["The diagram shows a 3x3x3 cube with the central small cube and the six face-centre small cubes removed.","The cutting plane goes through the centre and is perpendicular to a space diagonal so it can be represented by x+y+z=0 in a coordinate system with small-cube centres at (i,j,k) where i,j,k are -1,0,1.","A small cube centred at (i,j,k) intersects the plane when the range of x+y+z over that cube straddles 0, which occurs exactly when i+j+k is -1, 0, or 1.","There are 6 cubes with sum -1, 7 cubes with sum 0, and 6 cubes with sum 1, so 19 small cubes intersect the plane.","The seven removed cubes are the centre (sum 0) and the six face-centre cubes (sums ±1), so the removed cubes are exactly the central cluster of the 19 intersected cubes.","Removing that central cluster leaves the twelve outer intersected cubes forming a hexagonal annulus with a large regular hexagon outer boundary and a concentric smaller regular hexagonal hole.","The option that depicts a hexagon with a concentric hexagonal hole is B."], "answer": "B"}

{"reasoning_steps":["AD is a diameter so the circle center O is the midpoint of AD and the radius is R = AO = OD.","Inscribed angle BAC = 60° subtends arc BC of 120° so chord BC = 2R sin60° = R√3.","In triangle ABC the area equals (1/2)*AC*BE and also equals (1/2)*AB*AC*sin60°, so BE = AB*sin60°.","Using AB = 24 gives BE = 24*sin60° = 12√3 cm.","E lies on AC with EC = 3 and BE ⟂ AC, so BC^2 = BE^2 + EC^2 by the Pythagorean theorem.","Compute BC^2 = (12√3)^2 + 3^2 = 432 + 9 = 441 so BC = 21 cm.","From BC = R√3 we get R = 21/√3 = 7√3 cm.","For chord AB let the half central angle between A and B be θ, then AB = 2R sinθ so sinθ = AB/(2R) = 24/(2R) = 12/R = (4√3)/7.","Thus cosθ = sqrt(1 - sin^2θ) = sqrt(1 - 48/49) = 1/7.","Chord BD spans a central angle of π - 2θ so its length is BD = 2R cosθ = 2*(7√3)*(1/7) = 2√3 cm."],"answer":"D"}

{"reasoning_steps": ["The figure shows eight outer positions arranged around a central position with four diameters passing through the center.", "Each diameter contains two opposite outer positions and the central position so its three numbers sum to 24.", "Let the nine consecutive numbers be n through n+8.", "Let C denote the center number.", "For each diameter the opposite outer numbers sum to 24 minus C.", "Hence the sum of the eight outer numbers is 4*(24-C)=96-4C.", "Therefore the total sum of the nine numbers equals C+(96-4C)=96-3C.", "The total sum also equals 9n+36 because the numbers are n through n+8.", "Equating those expressions gives 96-3C=9n+36.", "That equation simplifies to C=20-3n.", "C must be one of the nine numbers so n<=20-3n<=n+8.", "Solving that inequality gives n in {3,4,5}.", "For n=3 the nine numbers are 3 through 11 and C=11.", "The outer pairs 3+10,4+9,5+8,6+7 each sum to 13.", "Each diameter then sums to 13+11=24 for n=3.", "For n=4 the nine numbers are 4 through 12 and C=8.", "The outer pairs 4+12,5+11,6+10,7+9 each sum to 16.", "Each diameter then sums to 16+8=24 for n=4.", "For n=5 the nine numbers are 5 through 13 and C=5.", "The outer pairs 6+13,7+12,8+11,9+10 each sum to 19.", "Each diameter then sums to 19+5=24 for n=5.", "The corresponding total sums are 63 for n=3, 72 for n=4, and 81 for n=5.", "Therefore the largest possible total sum is 81."], "answer": "81"}

{"reasoning_steps":["The figure shows a square divided into four triangles that meet at an interior point labeled A, B, C, D.","The square's area is 1 m^2 so each side length equals 1 m.","Each triangle has a side of the square as base and the perpendicular distance from the interior point to that side as height so each area equals (1 * distance)/2.","Therefore each perpendicular distance equals twice the corresponding triangle area.","Distances to opposite sides sum to the side length so A + B = 1/2 and C + D = 1/2.","The given ratios 3A = 4B and 2C = 3D imply A = 4B/3 and C = 3D/2.","From A + B = 1/2 and A = 4B/3 we get 7B/3 = 1/2 so B = 3/14 and A = 2/7.","From C + D = 1/2 and C = 3D/2 we get 5D/2 = 1/2 so D = 1/5 and C = 3/10.","The smallest area is D = 1/5 so the nearest side distance equals 2 * D = 2/5 m = 0.4 m.","The fly therefore flies 40 cm to the closest side."], "answer":"A"}

{"reasoning_steps":["The diagram shows three adjacent squares on a common baseline with side lengths 3 cm, 5 cm, and 8 cm from left to right.","A diagonal line runs from the bottom-left corner of the leftmost square to the top-right corner of the rightmost square.","Set a coordinate system with the baseline as y=0.","The leftmost square occupies x from 0 to 3.","The middle square occupies x from 3 to 8.","The rightmost square occupies x from 8 to 16.","The diagonal connects (0,0) and (16,8), so its equation is y = (1/2)x.","At x = 3 the diagonal height is y = (1/2)*3 = 1.5 cm.","At x = 8 the diagonal height is y = (1/2)*8 = 4 cm.","The shaded region inside the middle square is a trapezium with vertical parallel sides of lengths 1.5 cm and 4 cm and horizontal separation 5 cm.","The area is (1/2)*(1.5+4)*5 = 55/4 cm^2 by the trapezoid area formula.","Therefore the correct choice is B."], "answer":"B"}

{"reasoning_steps":["Triangle ABC is equilateral (given in the diagram).","Triangles AEF, DFE and CDF are congruent isosceles triangles (given).","F is the interior point on AC where the three congruent triangles meet (visible in the diagram).","Let the side length of equilateral triangle ABC be a.","Let each congruent isosceles triangle have equal sides of length p and base of length u, with the bases of triangles AEF and CDF being AF and CF respectively (consistent with the diagram).","AF and CF are the two bases and satisfy AF + CF = AC = a, so AF = CF = u and hence u = a/2.","The perimeter of one isosceles triangle is 2p + u and this equals the perimeter of ABC which is 3a, so 2p + u = 3a.","Substituting u = a/2 into 2p + u = 3a gives 2p + a/2 = 3a and hence p = 5a/4.","The pentagon perimeter is AB + BC + CD + DE + EA = a + a + p + u + p = 2a + 2p + u, which with p = 5a/4 and u = a/2 equals 5a, so the ratio is 5a / 3a = 5/3."], "answer": "D"}

{"reasoning_steps": ["The diagram shows the old tower partitioned into consecutive triples taken from the top such as 90,89,88 then 87,86,85 and so on.", "Each triple is placed onto the new tower without changing the triple's internal order.", "Placing successive triples on top therefore reverses the order of the triples relative to the original tower.", "Thus the new tower from top to bottom lists triples as 3,2,1 then 6,5,4 then 9,8,7 and so on in the form (3k,3k-1,3k-2).", "The number 39 is exactly 3*13 so it is the first element of triple k=13.", "The number 40 satisfies ceil(40/3)=14 so it is the third element of triple k=14.", "In the new tower 39 is at position 3*(13-1)+1 = 37 from the top.", "In the new tower 40 is at position 3*(14-1)+3 = 42 from the top.", "The number of blocks strictly between them is 42 - 37 - 1 = 4."], "answer": "4"}

{"reasoning_steps":["The problem statement gives the staircase has 2023 steps.","The problem statement gives that every third step is coloured black.","Black steps therefore correspond to step numbers divisible by 3.","The count of multiples of 3 from 1 to 2023 is floor(2023/3) = 674.","Those black steps can be written as 3k for k = 1 to 674.","Because 3 is odd the parity of 3k matches the parity of k.","Among k = 1 to 674 there are 337 odd k and 337 even k.","Therefore there are 337 black steps with odd indices and 337 black steps with even indices.","With alternate stepping the right foot lands on either all odd-numbered steps or all even-numbered steps depending on starting foot.","Therefore the right foot must land on 337 black steps regardless of starting foot."],"answer":"337"}

{"reasoning_steps": ["The large square is 30 cm on a side and is divided into a 3x3 grid of equal small squares as shown.", "Each small square therefore has side length 10 cm and area 100 cm^2.", "The shaded grey regions include three full small squares: the center square and the two bottom-left and bottom-middle squares as visible.", "There are two small grey disks drawn in the top-left and top-right small squares with radii 4 cm and 3 cm respectively as labeled.", "A large white circle of radius 5 cm is centered at the intersection of the vertical grid line and horizontal grid line between the middle and right/bottom squares as indicated by the symmetric overlap across four small squares.", "Because the radius is 5 cm and the circle is centered on that grid intersection, exactly one quarter of the white circle lies in the center small square and one quarter lies in the bottom-middle small square by symmetry.", "The combined area of the two small grey disks is 16π + 9π = 25π cm^2.", "The portion of the white circle overlapping the shaded squares equals half the white circle area, i.e. (1/2)·π·5^2 = 12.5π cm^2.", "The total shaded area equals the three full small squares plus the two small grey disks minus the white circle overlap, i.e. 300 + 25π - 12.5π = 300 + 12.5π cm^2."], "answer": "300 + (25/2)π cm^2"}

{"reasoning_steps": ["The image shows a single row of nine contiguous squares.", "The fifth square from the left contains the digit 3 as visible in the diagram.", "The seventh square from the left contains the digit 1 as visible in the diagram.", "Let b_i be the entries reduced mod 3, then the condition reads b_i+b_{i+1}+b_{i+2} ≡ 0 (mod 3) for all valid i.", "Subtracting consecutive triple-sum equations gives b_{i+3} ≡ b_i (mod 3) for all valid i, so residues repeat every three positions.", "Therefore positions 1,4,7 share one residue class, positions 2,5,8 share a second residue class, and positions 3,6,9 share a third residue class.", "The digit 3 at position 5 shows that positions 2,5,8 must have residue 0 (mod 3).", "The digit 1 at position 7 shows that positions 1,4,7 must have residue 1 (mod 3).", "The remaining residue for positions 3,6,9 must be 2 (mod 3) because 1+0+2 ≡ 0 (mod 3).", "The numbers congruent to 0 mod 3 are {3,6,9} and with 3 fixed at position 5 the remaining two {6,9} can be placed in positions 2 and 8 in 2! = 2 ways.", "The numbers congruent to 1 mod 3 are {1,4,7} and with 1 fixed at position 7 the remaining two {4,7} can be placed in positions 1 and 4 in 2! = 2 ways.", "The numbers congruent to 2 mod 3 are {2,5,8} and they can be arranged among positions 3,6,9 in 3! = 6 ways.", "The total number of valid placements is the product 2*2*6 = 24."], "answer": "24"}

{"reasoning_steps":["There are seven circles arranged in a T-shape with three across the top, three across the middle, and one centered below the middle.","The problem statement says the product of the three numbers on each straight line (the top horizontal, the middle horizontal, and the central vertical) is the same.","Label the circles A B C on the top row left-to-right, D E F on the middle row left-to-right, and G on the bottom-center.","The equality of the three line-products gives A*B*C = D*E*F = B*E*G.","Cancelling the common factors yields A*C = E*G and D*F = B*G.","All seven numbers are pairwise different single-digit numbers according to the statement.","Hence E*G must admit two different representations as products of distinct single-digit factors, which restricts E*G to values in {6,8,12,18,24} when factors are taken from 1..9.","Exhaustive checking of those possibilities and the remaining digit-factor pairs from 1..9 produces no assignment of seven distinct digits that satisfies both A*C = E*G and D*F = B*G simultaneously.","Therefore under the usual interpretation (pairwise different positive single-digit integers 1–9) the given conditions do not determine a unique valid digit for the bottom circle."],"answer":"insufficient information"}

{"reasoning_steps":["The diagram shows two parallel horizontal diameters labeled A B (bottom) and C D (top).","Marks labeled \"1\" on the picture indicate each semicircle has radius 1 and each diameter has length 2.","Each semicircle's center is at the midpoint of its diameter on the corresponding horizontal line.","The problem statement and diagram show the extension of each diameter is tangent to the opposite semicircle.","Tangency of the lower diameter line to the upper circle implies the vertical distance between the two diameter lines equals 1.","Thus the centers of the two semicircles are separated vertically by 1.","The two semicircles appear externally tangent to each other which implies the distance between their centers equals the sum of radii, 2.","By the Pythagorean theorem the horizontal separation of the centers is sqrt(2^2-1^2)=sqrt(3).","Placing the lower center at x=0 gives A at x=-1 and the upper center at x=sqrt(3) so D is at x=sqrt(3)+1 and the vertical difference is 1.","The vector from A to D is (sqrt(3)+2,1) so AD^2=(sqrt(3)+2)^2+1^2.","Algebraic simplification yields AD^2=8+4*sqrt(3)."], "answer":"B"}

{"reasoning_steps":["The image shows a 3x3 grid with 1 at top-left, 3 at top-right, 2 at bottom-left, and 4 at bottom-right.","The five empty cells therefore must contain the digits 5,6,7,8,9.","If 9 were in the center then its four neighbours would be the four edge cells and they would sum to 5+6+7+8=26, not 15.","If 9 were at the top-middle then its neighbours would be 1, 3, and the center and thus the center would be 15-1-3=11, which is impossible.","If 9 were at the left-middle then its neighbours would be 1, 2, and the center and thus the center would be 15-1-2=12, which is impossible.","If 9 were at the bottom-middle then its neighbours would be 2, 4, and the center and thus the center would be 15-2-4=9, which duplicates 9 and is impossible.","Therefore 9 must be at the right-middle where its neighbours are 3, 4, and the center and thus the center must be 15-3-4=8.","Thus the center contains 8 and its four neighbours are the three remaining edge cells 5, 6, 7 and the cell with 9.","Therefore the sum of the neighbours of 8 is 9+5+6+7=27."], "answer":"27"}

{"reasoning_steps": ["The diagram shows PQ vertical and PS horizontal meeting at P which indicates a right angle at P.", "The diagram shows PQ vertical and QR horizontal meeting at Q which indicates a right angle at Q.", "The diagonals PR and QS cross at an interior point X as shown.", "The areas labeled 10 and 5 appear in the triangles PQX and PXS respectively.", "Place coordinates P(0,h), Q(0,0), S(s,h), and R(r,0) which fits the visible horizontals and verticals.", "The intersection X of PR and QS has coordinates (rs/(r+s), hr/(r+s)) by solving the line equations.", "The area of triangle PQX equals (1/2)*h*(rs/(r+s)) which is given as 10.", "The area of triangle PXS equals (1/2)*h*(s^2/(r+s)) which is given as 5.", "Dividing these area formulas gives s/r = 5/10 = 1/2.", "Substituting s = r/2 gives the other two triangle areas as 20 and 10 respectively.", "The total area of quadrilateral PQRS is 10 + 5 + 20 + 10 = 45 cm^2."], "answer": "45 cm^2"}

{"reasoning_steps": ["Read text: \"abc + acb = c4a\" as shown in the image.", "a, b, c are distinct digits and a and c are nonzero because they appear as hundreds digits in three-digit numbers.", "Translate to numbers: 100a+10b+c + 100a+10c+b = 100c+40+a.", "Simplify to 199a + 11b = 89c + 40.", "Reduce mod 11 to get a ≡ c + 7 (mod 11), which for digits 0–9 gives a = c + 7 or a = c - 4.", "Substituting a = c + 7 with c = 0,1,2 produces b outside 0–9, so that family is impossible.", "Substituting a = c - 4 into the simplified equation yields b = 76 - 10c.", "Testing c = 5..9 gives only c = 7 with b = 6 and a = 3 as valid distinct digits in 0–9.", "Verify 367 + 376 = 743 which matches c4a = 743 from the image.", "Therefore a + b + c = 3 + 6 + 7 = 16."], "answer": "16"}

{"reasoning_steps": ["The diagram shows rectangle PRSV with PR labeled 20 cm and PV labeled 12 cm.", "Points U and T lie on the top edge VS and point Q lies on the bottom edge PR as shown.", "Diagonal segments connect P to U, Q to U, Q to T, and T to R forming two white triangular regions and the shaded remainder.", "The two white regions are triangles with their apexes on the top edge at U and T and their bases on the bottom edge at segments PQ and QR respectively.", "Each white triangle therefore has height equal to the rectangle height 12 cm because their apexes are on the top edge and bases on the bottom edge.", "The combined area of the two white triangles is (1/2)*12*(PQ) + (1/2)*12*(QR) = 6*(PQ+QR).", "Point Q lies between P and R so PQ + QR = PR = 20 cm as visible on the bottom edge.", "Thus the combined white area is 6*20 = 120 cm^2.", "The rectangle area is 20*12 = 240 cm^2, and the shaded area is rectangle area minus white area = 240 - 120 = 120 cm^2."], "answer": "E"}

{"reasoning_steps": ["The picture shows four vertical rectangles of equal horizontal width placed side-by-side in each arrangement.", "The width of each rectangle is 10 cm as given.", "The ribbon lengths increase by 25 cm steps as given.", "Let the lengths be a, a+25, a+50, a+75 from shortest to longest.", "In the left diagram the ribbons are ordered left-to-right increasingly by length as visible.", "The union perimeter equals the sum of the rectangles' perimeters minus twice the lengths of the internal shared vertical contacts.", "The sum of individual perimeters is 2*(sum of lengths) + 8*width.", "For the left increasing order the three internal shared contacts equal a, a+25, and a+50.", "Substituting those values into the perimeter formula gives the left perimeter P1 = 2*(4a+150) + 8*10 - 2*(3a+75).", "That expression simplifies to P1 = 2a + 230 cm.", "In the right diagram the leftmost rectangle is the second-longest and the second rectangle is the longest as seen by their relative top heights.", "The third rectangle is the shortest and the fourth is the second-shortest as seen by their relative top heights.", "For that right order the internal shared contacts are a+50, a, and a, giving sum 3a + 50.", "Substituting into the perimeter formula gives the right perimeter P2 = 2*(4a+150) + 8*10 - 2*(3a+50).", "That expression simplifies to P2 = 2a + 280 cm.", "Therefore the difference P2 - P1 = (2a + 280) - (2a + 230) = 50 cm.", "The correct multiple-choice answer is option B."], "answer": "B"}

{"reasoning_steps":["The diagram shows square PQRS with side PS equal to 10 cm.","P, S, R, Q are arranged clockwise at top-left, top-right, bottom-right, bottom-left respectively.","Triangle PST has angles at P and S given as angle SPT = 75° and angle TSP = 30°.","The third angle at T in triangle PST equals 180° - 75° - 30° = 75°.","Triangle PST therefore has angles 75°, 30°, and 75°.","In triangle PST the sides opposite equal angles are equal, so ST = PS.","PS is a side of the square and equals 10 cm, so ST = 10 cm.","SR is also a side of the square and equals 10 cm.","Angle RSP equals 90° and angle TSP equals 30°, so the angle RST equals 90° - 30° = 60°.","Applying the cosine law to triangle SRT with SR = ST = 10 cm and included angle 60° gives TR^2 = 10^2 + 10^2 - 2*10*10*cos60° = 100."],"answer":"E"}

{"reasoning_steps": ["The diagram shows two congruent squares PQRS and WXYZ with corresponding sides parallel and overlapping symmetrically.", "Each square's corner appears to lie at the midpoint of a side of the other square, so each square is shifted by half a side relative to the other.", "This shift makes the overlapping shaded region decompose into four congruent right triangles formed by connecting those midpoints.", "If A is the area of one square then each of those four triangles has area A/8 and the shaded area is 4*(A/8)=A/2.", "The shaded area is given as 1 cm^2 so A/2 = 1 cm^2 and hence A = 2 cm^2."], "answer": "B"}

{"reasoning_steps": ["The visible front faces of the two bottom dice are 1 (left) and 2 (right).", "The visible right faces of the bottom-right and top-right dice are 3 (lower) and 4 (upper) respectively.", "The visible top face of the top-right die is 6.", "On a standard die opposite faces sum to 7.", "From the bottom-right right face 3, its left face is 4 by the opposite-face rule.", "Because the two bottom dice touch, the bottom-left right face equals that 4, so the bottom-left right face is 4.", "From the top-right right face 4, its left face is 3 by the opposite-face rule.", "Because the two top dice touch, the top-left right face equals that 3, so the top-left right face is 3.", "From the top-right top face 6, its bottom face is 1 by the opposite-face rule.", "Because the top-right bottom touches the bottom-right top, the bottom-right top face is 1.", "Considering the bottom-right die has front 2 and top 1 and right 3, this is the canonical orientation and the top-right die is that die flipped, consistent with the visible 4 and 6.", "The bottom-left die has front 1 and right 4, and rotating a standard die to put 1 in front and 4 on the right yields top = 2.", "Because the bottom-left top touches the top-left bottom, the top-left bottom is 2.", "By the opposite-face rule the top-left top face is 5."], "answer": "5"}

{"reasoning_steps": ["The diagram shows PQ and PR with matching ticks, so PQ = PR.", "The diagram shows QS and PS with matching ticks, so QS = PS.", "Point S is on segment QR as shown by its placement on the base line QR.", "The labeled angle at P between PR and PS is 75°, so ∠RPS = 75°.", "Let α denote apex angle ∠QPR of isosceles triangle PQR.", "Then the base angles ∠PQR and ∠QRP equal (180°−α)/2.", "PS lies between PQ and PR at the apex, so ∠QPS = α−75°.", "Since QS = PS, triangle QPS is isosceles with vertex at S.", "Therefore ∠QPS equals ∠PQS.", "Angle ∠PQS equals ∠PQR because QS is collinear with QR on the base.", "Thus α−75° = (180°−α)/2.", "Solving gives α = 110° and hence ∠QRP = (180°−110°)/2 = 35°."], "answer": "A"}

{"reasoning_steps":["The image shows a 2x2 square grid with four cells.","The second row corresponds to the bottom two cells.","The second column corresponds to the right two cells.","Label the cells TL, TR, BL, BR for top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right.","The problem gives BL + BR = 6.","The problem gives TR + BR = 10.","Subtracting those equations gives TR - BL = 4.","Therefore BL = TR - 4.","The four entries are distinct and are 2, 3, 4 and an unknown x.","If TR = x then BR = 10 - x and BL = x - 4.","BR and BL must be two distinct numbers from the set {2,3,4}.","If 10 - x = 2 then x = 8.","If x = 8 then BL = x - 4 = 4.","If BR = 2 and BL = 4 then TL must be the remaining number 3.","If 10 - x = 4 then x = 6.","If x = 6 then BL = x - 4 = 2.","If BR = 4 and BL = 2 then TL must be the remaining number 3.","Both valid assignments yield TL = 3."], "answer": "3"}

{"reasoning_steps":["The figure shows a square with a triangle attached along the square's top side.","The triangle's base coincides with the square's top side as seen in the image.","Let the square side length be s as a variable.","The square perimeter is 4s from its four equal sides.","The problem states the triangle perimeter equals the square perimeter, so the triangle perimeter is 4s.","The triangle's perimeter equals base s plus the sum of the two other sides, so the two other sides sum to 3s.","The pentagon's boundary is the union of the square and triangle boundaries minus the shared side counted twice.","Therefore the pentagon perimeter equals 4s + 4s - 2s = 6s.","The ratio of pentagon perimeter to square perimeter is 6s to 4s which simplifies to 3:2."],"answer":"B"}

{"reasoning_steps": ["The figure shows P and Q on a horizontal line with S between them and PS:SQ = 2:3.", "Set coordinates P=(0,0) and Q=(5,0) so S=(2,0).", "Let R=(x,y) with y>0 and let T = S + λ(R-S) for some λ in [0,1].", "The area of triangle PQR equals (1/2)*PQ*y = (5/2)*y.", "The area of triangle PTR equals y*(1-λ).", "The area of triangle SQT equals (3/2)*λ*y because SQ = 3. {"reasoning_steps":["The diagram shows two congruent squares stacked on the left and a third square attached to the right of the middle square, so the left-square side length is s and the right-square side length is t.","Route 2 follows the cycle A-B-C-F-G-H-A and traverses six left-square edges each of length s.","The problem statement gives Route 2 length 12 km so 6s = 12 km and s = 2 km.","Route 4 follows C-F-G-H-C and traverses four left-square edges forming the perimeter of one left square.","Therefore the length of Route 4 is 4s = 4 * 2 km = 8 km."],"answer":"C"}

{"reasoning_steps": ["Read text: 'KAN' on the top line, '+ GA' on the second line, and 'ROO' below the horizontal line.", "Interpret the figure as the cryptarithm KAN + GA = ROO with each letter a different digit and with leading letters nonzero.", "The ones column has carry c1 = 1.", "The tens column equation is A + G + 1 = O + 10*c2.", "Equating the ones and tens expressions gives N = G + 11 - 10*c2.", "This forces c2 = 1.", "Therefore N = G + 1.", "The hundreds column gives R = K + c2, so R = K + 1.", "Compute RN - KG = 10(R - K) + (N - G) = 10*1 + 1 = 11."], "answer": "11"}

{"reasoning_steps": ["The smallest square side is 20 cm as stated.", "Visually the left column stacks a small square, a medium square that is 2 smalls tall, and another small square giving a total height of 1+2+1 = 4 small units.", "Visibly the middle row shows a left medium that is 2 smalls wide, then three small squares across, then a right medium that is 2 smalls wide giving a total width of 2+3+2 = 7 small units.", "Therefore the outer rectangle measures 7 by 4 in units of the small square side.", "The perimeter of this outer rectangle is 2*(7+4) = 22 small-side lengths.", "The marked path from P to Q follows around three sides of the rectangle while cutting across two small-side segments as visible in the diagram, so the path length equals the perimeter minus 2 small-side lengths, i.e., 22-2 = 20 small-side lengths.", "Multiplying 20 small-side lengths by 20 cm per small side gives 20*20 cm = 400 cm."], "answer": "B"}

{"reasoning_steps":["Read text: \"N is divisible by 5\".","Read text: \"N is divisible by 11\".","Read text: \"N is divisible by 55\".","Read text: \"N is less than 10\".","Exactly two of the four given statements are true, per problem text.","If \"N is divisible by 55\" is true then both \"N is divisible by 5\" and \"N is divisible by 11\" are true.","Therefore \"N is divisible by 55\" cannot be true because that would make at least three statements true.","At most one of \"N is divisible by 5\" and \"N is divisible by 11\" can be true because if both were true then \"N is divisible by 55\" would be true.","To have exactly two true statements with \"N is divisible by 55\" false, exactly one of divisibility-by-5 or divisibility-by-11 must be true and \"N is less than 10\" must be true.","The positive integers less than 10 are 1 through 9.","Among 1 through 9 only 5 is divisible by 5 and none are divisible by 11.","Therefore N = 5."],"answer":"5"}

{"reasoning_steps": ["The diagram shows a square with labeled corners P (top-left), V (top-right), R (bottom-right) and Q (bottom-left).", "Set the square side length to 1 and place P=(0,1), V=(1,1), R=(1,0), Q=(0,0).", "The equilateral triangle has base PV and its third vertex W lies below PV inside the square.", "For base PV of length 1 the equilateral apex is at W=(0.5, 1 - sqrt(3)/2) which is approximately (0.5, 0.133974596).", "The regular pentagon shares side VR of length 1 with the square and proceeds clockwise R -> V -> U -> T -> S.", "The vector R->V is (0,1) so rotating it clockwise by 72° gives the vector V->U at angle 18°, hence U = V + (cos18°, sin18°) ≈ (1.951056516, 1.309016989).", "At vertex U the vectors to V and W are U->V = V - U ≈ (-0.951056516, -0.309016989) and U->W = W - U ≈ (-1.451056516, -1.175042393).", "The dot product of U->V and U->W is ≈1.74314475 and the product of their lengths is ≈1.86716, giving cosine ≈0.93386.", "arccos(0.93386) ≈ 21°, so angle WUV ≈ 21° which matches option A."], "answer": "A"}

{"reasoning_steps":["The top row contains a spade, a diamond, and a spade and shows the sum \"53\".","The middle row contains a diamond, a spade, and a club and shows the sum \"47\".","The bottom row contains a diamond, a club, and a spade and shows the sum \"47\".","The column sums shown below the grid read \"52\", \"47\", and \"48\" under the first, second, and third columns respectively.","Assign variables A = ♠, B = ♦, and C = ♣ based on the visible symbols.","The top-row equation from the visible symbols is 2A + B = 53.","The middle-row equation from the visible symbols is A + B + C = 47.","The first-column equation from the visible symbols is A + 2B = 52.","The third-column equation from the visible symbols is 2A + C = 48.","Solving A + 2B = 52 and 2A + B = 53 gives A = 18 and B = 17.","Substituting A = 18 into 2A + C = 48 gives C = 12.","The requested expression ♠ + ♦ − ♣ equals A + B − C = 18 + 17 − 12 = 23."], "answer":"23"}

{"reasoning_steps": ["PQRS is a square of side 10 cm as labeled.", "MN is the middle segment on the top side and MN = 6 cm as given.", "The two equal margins on the top side are (10-6)/2 = 2 cm so each small corner square has side 2 cm.", "The four congruent small corner squares therefore have total area 4*(2^2) = 16 cm^2.", "Each of the four isosceles triangles has base MN = 6 cm because their bases lie on the exposed middle segment of each side.", "The four triangle apices lie symmetrically and appear to form a centered smaller square of side 4, so the perpendicular distance (height) from a side to a triangle apex is (10-4)/2 = 3 cm.", "Each triangle therefore has area (1/2)*6*3 = 9 cm^2 and the four triangles have total area 36 cm^2.", "The shaded region area is 100 - 16 - 36 = 48 cm^2."], "answer": "C"}

{"reasoning_steps":["Image shows top entries 10, 13, 20, 26 and bottom entries 3, 7, 6, 14 in successive columns.","The second column entries 13 and 7 equal 10+3 and 10-3 respectively, matching the stated rule.","The third column entries 20 and 6 equal 13+7 and 13-7 respectively, confirming the rule across columns.","Applying the rule twice gives the third-column entries 20 and 6 which equal 2*10 and 2*3 respectively, so two steps double both entries.","Therefore applying two one-step transformations multiplies both entries by 2, so the two-step operator equals 2 times the identity.","A 2x7 table involves 6 one-step applications, which is three two-step applications.","Three two-step applications multiply the initial column by 2^3 = 8, so the final column equals 8 times the first column.","Carl's final column entries are 96 and 64 as given.","Thus the first column entries are 96/8 = 12 and 64/8 = 8.","Therefore the sum of the numbers in the first column is 20."],"answer":"20"}

{"reasoning_steps": ["Read text: 'All the eels are electric eels except 12'.", "Read text: 'All the eels are moray eels except 14'.", "Read text: 'All the eels are freshwater eels except 16'.", "Let N be the total number of eels in the tank.", "The number of electric eels is N - 12.", "The number of moray eels is N - 14.", "The number of freshwater eels is N - 16.", "Because every eel is exactly one type, (N - 12) + (N - 14) + (N - 16) equals N.", "Solving 3N - 42 = N gives N = 21.", "Therefore there are 21 eels in the tank."], "answer": "21"}

{"reasoning_steps":["The image shows a rectangular grid with 4 rows and 5 columns and the top row entries from left to right are R, B, (blank), Y, G as visible.","The cell marked X is the bottom-right cell (row 4, column 5) as visible.","The rule that any two cells sharing a vertex must be different implies every 2x2 block contains all four colours as a direct, visible consequence.","From the top-row Y (column 4) and G (column 5) the two cells immediately below them (row 2, columns 4 and 5) must be R and B in some order because each 2x2 must contain all four colours.","From the top-row R (column 1) and B (column 2) the two cells immediately below them (row 2, columns 1 and 2) must be Y and G in some order because each 2x2 must contain all four colours.","Cell (1,3) must be either R or G because it shares vertices with the visible B at (1,2) and Y at (1,4) and hence cannot be B or Y.","Assuming (1,3)=R, repeated application of the 2x2-all-colours rule forces (2,4)=B, (2,5)=R, (2,3)=G, (2,2)=Y, (3,4)=Y, (3,3)=R, (4,4)=B and therefore X=(4,5)=R.","Assuming (1,3)=G, repeated application of the 2x2-all-colours rule forces (2,4)=B, (2,5)=R, (2,3)=R, (2,2)=Y, (3,2)=B, (3,3)=G, (3,4)=Y, (4,2)=Y, (4,3)=R, (4,4)=B and therefore X=(4,5)=R.","Both possible colours for (1,3) lead to the same forced colour R for X so the colour of X is uniquely determined as R."], "answer": "A"}

{"reasoning_steps":["Option C shows a 2x4 grid with rows top-to-bottom reading (O,O), (K,R), (A,A), (G,N).","I label columns left=1 right=2 and rows top=1 bottom=4 to give coordinates (col,row).","The parity color of a cell is (col+row) mod 2.","A king move (sharing a vertex) always changes the parity color of the cell.","Therefore letters in odd positions 1,3,5,7 of the word must occupy cells of the same parity color and letters in even positions 2,4,6,8 must occupy the opposite parity color.","In option C the letters occupy coordinates and parities: (1,1)=O parity0.","(2,1)=O parity1.","(1,2)=K parity1.","(2,2)=R parity0.","(1,3)=A parity0.","(2,3)=A parity1.","(1,4)=G parity1.","(2,4)=N parity0.","The odd-index letters in the word are K (index1), N (3), A (5), O (7).","In option C those odd-index letters appear at parities: K parity1, N parity0, A parity0, O parity0.","Because the odd-index letters do not all lie on the same parity color in option C it is impossible to place the word by successive king moves."],"answer":"C"}

{"reasoning_steps": ["The shaded region is the quadrilateral with vertices Q, T, S, W as shown in the diagram.", "T is the midpoint of PS and W is the midpoint of SR as labeled on the figure.", "I place the rhombus at coordinates P(0,1), Q(-1,0), R(0,-1), S(1,0) to match the drawn diamond shape and preserve midpoints.", "The midpoint T of P and S is (0.5,0.5).", "The midpoint W of S and R is (0.5,-0.5).", "The shaded quadrilateral Q-T-S-W therefore has coordinates (-1,0), (0.5,0.5), (1,0), (0.5,-0.5).", "Applying the shoelace formula gives the shaded area as 1 unit^2.", "Applying the shoelace formula to P,Q,R,S gives the total rhombus area as 2 unit^2.", "Thus the unshaded area is 1 unit^2 and the ratio unshaded:shaded is 1:1."], "answer": "A"}

{"reasoning_steps":["I see five distinct city dots in the map.","A complete network among five cities requires C(5,2)=10 roads.","There is a visible road between the top city and the left city.","There is a visible road between the top city and the lower-left city.","There is a visible road between the top city and the lower-right city.","There is a visible diagonal road between the left city and the lower-right city.","There is a visible road between the lower-left city and the lower-right city.","There is a visible short road between the lower-right city and the right city.","No visible road connects the top city to the right city.","No visible road connects the left city to the right city.","No visible road connects the left city to the lower-left city.","No visible road connects the lower-left city to the right city.","I count six visible roads.","Ten required minus six visible gives four missing roads."],"answer":"4"}

{"reasoning_steps": ["The rectangle is given as 5 cm by 10 cm.", "The large quarter circles have diameters that visually match the 10 cm side, so each large quarter has radius 5 cm.", "The small quarter circles have diameters that visually match the 5 cm side, so each small quarter has radius 2.5 cm.", "A large semicircle made from the two large quarters has arc length 5π cm (since semicircle arc = πr with r=5).", "A small semicircle made from the two small quarters has arc length 2.5π cm (since semicircle arc = πr with r=2.5).", "The right diagram clearly shows the large semicircular arc and the two small quarter arcs all exposed on the outer boundary and three exposed straight segments summing to 10 cm, so its visible perimeter equals 10 + 7.5π cm.", "The left diagram’s assembly of the same five pieces is visually ambiguous about which straight edges of the rectangle are covered by quarter-circle pieces and which rectangle edges remain exposed, so the total exposed straight length cannot be determined unambiguously from the image alone."], "answer": "insufficient information"}

{"reasoning_steps": ["Points P, Q, R are collinear on the left slanted line as shown.", "Points P, T, S are collinear on the slanted top-right line as shown.", "Arrow marks on QT and RS indicate QT is parallel to RS.", "Tick marks on PQ and QT indicate PQ equals QT.", "The diagram gives angle STQ = 154°.", "Because PT and ST are opposite rays at T, angle PTQ = 180° - 154° = 26°.", "In triangle PQT the equal sides PQ and QT imply angle QPT = angle PTQ = 26°.", "Thus angle PQT = 180° - (26° + 26°) = 128°.", "RQ is the extension of QP so angle RQT = 180° - angle PQT = 52°.", "Because RS is parallel to QT and RQ is opposite QR, angle SRQ = 180° - angle RQT = 128°."], "answer": "E"}

{"reasoning_steps":["The figure is a regular octagon folded exactly in half three times so there are 2^3 = 8 layers in the folded triangle.","Each of the 8 layers corresponds to one of the eight sectors of the original octagon and will be affected by the same cut when unfolded.","A single cut made on the stacked triangle will be reflected into 8 congruent cuts in the unfolded octagon by the three fold reflections.","Reflections across the fold lines produce the 8 cuts as four pairs of opposite, parallel cuts when mapped back to the octagon.","The intersections of those four pairs of parallel cuts form a small centered quadrilateral with four right angles, i.e., a square, in the octagon.","Option C visually shows a small centered square inside the octagon that matches the described set of reflected cuts."], "answer":"C"}

{"reasoning_steps":["The diagram shows a rectangle subdivided into four smaller rectangles by one vertical and one horizontal line.","Let the left and right widths be a and b and the top and bottom heights be c and d.","The perimeters of the four small rectangles are 2(a+c), 2(b+c), 2(a+d), and 2(b+d).","Opposite small rectangles have perimeters that sum to 2(a+b+c+d), which equals the perimeter of WXYZ.","Three given small perimeters are 11, 16, and 19 and the fourth perimeter x is between 11 and 19.","The four perimeters must pair into two equal sums that each equal the large perimeter.","If 11 pairs with 16 the sum is 27.","Then 19 + x = 27.","8 is not between 11 and 19.","If 11 pairs with x then 16 + 19 = 35.","Then x = 24.","24 is not between 11 and 19.","If 11 pairs with 19 the sum is 30.","Then 16 + x = 30.","Hence x = 14.","14 lies between 11 and 19.","Therefore the perimeter of WXYZ equals 30."], "answer": "30"}

{"reasoning_steps":["Option A shows row counts 4,2,1,1 and column counts 0,3,3,2 as read from the image.","Option A row total 4+2+1+1 equals 8 and column total 0+3+3+2 equals 8 so totals match visually.","Option A is impossible because a row count of 4 requires a painted cell in every column which contradicts the visible column count 0 for the first column.","Option B shows row counts 1,2,1,3 and column counts 2,2,3,1 as read from the image.","Option B is impossible because the visible row total 1+2+1+3 equals 7 and the visible column total 2+2+3+1 equals 8 which do not match.","Option C shows row counts 3,3,0,0 and column counts 1,3,1,1 as read from the image.","Option C is impossible because only two rows contain painted cells but the visible second column count is 3 which exceeds the number of nonempty rows.","Option D shows row counts 2,1,2,2 and column counts 2,1,2,2 as read from the image.","Option D is feasible and one explicit placement consistent with the visible counts is row1 painted in columns 1 and 3, row2 painted in column 2, row3 painted in columns 1 and 4, and row4 painted in columns 3 and 4.","Option E shows row counts 0,3,1,3 and column counts 0,3,1,3 as read from the image.","Option E is impossible because a visible row count of 3 requires a painted cell in the first column which contradicts the visible column count 0 for the first column."],"answer":"D"}

{"reasoning_steps": ["The image shows seven circles arranged in a triangle with one at the top, three in a middle row, and three in a bottom row.", "There are five straight lines of three aligned circles: the left slanted line through the apex, the vertical line through the apex, the right slanted line through the apex, the middle horizontal line, and the bottom horizontal line.", "Label the apex circle A, the middle row left-to-right B, C, D, and the bottom row left-to-right E, F, G.", "Each of the five lines must have the same sum S.", "The apex circle A lies on three of these lines and each other circle lies on two lines, as shown by the connections.", "Summing the five line sums gives 5S = 3A + 2(B+C+D+E+F+G).", "The seven numbers sum to 1+2+3+4+5+6+7 = 28, so 5S = 3A + 2(28 - A) = A + 56.", "A + 56 must be divisible by 5 and this holds only for A = 4, giving S = 12.", "Therefore the apex circle must contain 4."], "answer": "4"}

{"reasoning_steps": ["The original square has area 64 cm^2.", "Therefore the side length of the square is 8 cm.", "The first fold is along the vertical midline and folds the left half onto the right half as shown by the arrow.", "After the first fold the outer shape is the right half of the square which is a rectangle 4 cm by 8 cm.", "The second fold is along the slanted crease shown from the top of that rectangle to about the midpoint of its right side.", "That second fold produces the thin vertical strip on the right whose width equals half the folded rectangle's width, which is 2 cm.", "The two shaded rectangles together occupy that strip for its full height of 8 cm as indicated by the shaded portions matching the strip width.", "Therefore the combined area of the two shaded rectangles is 2 cm * 8 cm = 16 cm^2."], "answer": "D"}

{"reasoning_steps": ["The image shows two adjacent blank square boxes followed by a multiplication sign and a single blank square box equals 176.", "This represents a two-digit number with repeated digits multiplied by the same single digit equals 176.", "A two-digit number with repeated digit d can be written as 11·d.", "Multiplying that by the same digit gives 11·d^2 = 176.", "Solving yields d^2 = 176/11 = 16.", "Therefore d = 4 as a single-digit nonnegative solution.", "Verification shows 44 × 4 = 176 which matches the image's result."], "answer": "4"}
